An expression of confusion making its way onto your face as you looked at your colleague with furrowed brows.“What?” The singular word was all that came from you in response. They came out with just the right amount of conviction, and without hesitation.
“You-you’re right…” She managed to stutter out, her face now flushed from shame. “I shouldn’t have jumped to conclusions.” She muttered before scurrying off to busy herself with something else. Hopefully, she realized there were more important things to do before a stadium performance than gossip. Speaking of important things, you still needed to do Mira’s makeup before sound check. You quickly gathered your supplies and made your way towards the dressing rooms. Little did you know a certain someone had overheard your conversation.

As time went on she had gotten pretty good at pretending to be unbothered by it, but deep down insecurity still quietly ate at her.But this new feeling that was spreading through her chest wasn’t one she was at all familiar with. She sat in her white robe looking at herself in the mirror trying to figure out what to say when she saw you. Yes she had heard your conversation with Lua, but more importantly, she had heard you defend her. You had spoken so confidently about her being a person worth getting to know. However, what really struck her was what you said about being different isn’t the same as being difficult. Well, it had Mira’s face flushing and heart racing in a way she had never experienced before. A polite voice came through from the other side, asking to be let in. So much for having more time before having to face you.
From the moment you walked in, you had noticed Mira was acting noticeably off. She was oddly jumpy, and every time your faces were close together she'd avert her eyes. Furthermore, every time your back was turned you could feel her gaze boring into your figure. It never felt hateful but you’d be lying if you said it wasn’t making you a little worried. Yet he kept repeating to himself that none of this had to do with Bill. Definitely not the fact that the mere mention of Hillary's name would awaken a furious jealousy within him. Definitely not the fact that at every debate his eyes would ravage the room in his search for the slightest hint of Bill, and perhaps with a half-hidden urge to ravage him just as well.So he kept repeating these things to himself, until he somehow managed to convince himself that he wouldn't even need Bill to fill in the hole in his heart, and mouth. He repeated it so well in fact that he finally managed to convince himself of it, and now he had all he could ever want. Everything except for Bill.Donald closed his eyes, finally realized the truth of it all. Without Bill, without that big beautiful.... Bill, everything amounted to nothing.

“Can you help us find a door with three windows?”Riley knew this song and dance by now. The answer -the real one that would shut down the emergency response system and potentially save their enby hide from the Shepard pounding on the door- was something they needed to either manipulate in this room or in the pods behind them.With how frantic Chicken Scratch was, pointing to both the sun and a nearby tree, the opossum had seen others fail this before.Riley looked around the immediate area. Nothing on the computer console or monitor itself. The shelves where they had uncovered an important tape didn’t have any odd symbols on it either. In a half walk, half panicked jog, Riley went back out to the life support pods. The alarm sirens were much louder out here.Looking over the pods, the sirens were making it hard to think. Knowing that a monster was waiting on the other end of the door instilled some sense of urgency. But Riley needed to think. Riley didn’t have the time to think. What were they missing…?Come on Riley, you can figure this out. You’ve figured all the rest out until now. Aunt Kate is either rolling in her grave or cheering you on as we speak.“Come on, Riley,” Amanda sang, loud enough to be heard over the sirens, “Being a secret spy isn’t that har-rd.”Riley whipped their head around to where the security console was. They moved to the left of the room so the console was in eyerange just to angrily sign;“Calm down for 5 minutes, Carrie White. It’s too fucking loud to think right now.”On the monitor, everything froze. Even the sirens seemed to putter out for a moment, and stopped for a breath or two. Wooly’s eyes grew wide, a small flicker going to Amanda before looking back out again. Chicken Scratch lowered their arms just to tilt their head in confusion. Amanda just… stared.“What did you just call me?”Riley’s heart nearly stopped right then and there. Did they really just compare Amanda to horror’s most infamously traumatized telekinetic? There was already one demonic monster out for Riley’s toasted rear, would they even survive if the second showed up?“Oh, you’re just filled with jokes, aren’t you Riley?” Amanda then laughed, breaking the tense spell over the area. “Secret agents can be so serious. But not you!”Riley let out a long, grateful sigh. Jesus, this girl…“Uh… Don’t forget our list.” Wooly reminded them both. “We’re still looking for a house with three windows.”The reminder of the scavenger hunt list brought Chicken Scratch back to attention as well. Even more frantic than before, they stretched their arms as far as they could at the tree and sun once more.Back on a timer, Riley looked back to the pods. That was when they noticed something on the side displays. Riley tilted their head. Then they noticed the power cables connecting to a breaker switch.Huh.Maybe being a secret spy wasn’t that hard after all…

I don't know, there's not much to say about it. It's hardly even worth a diary entry.It's still burning, owing in no small part to the fact that it's been rustling under the sleeve of my hoodie all day. I went out to dinner with my parents, which I didn't at all expect to do when I was panting and sweating in a bathroom stall, smothering the cuts with toilet paper. So, when I rolled up my sleeves to enjoy the katsudon they bought for me, I had to be... quite conscious of that.It swirls me with a guilt that I shouldn't have to think about, because they never saw and were therefore never hurt. That's the issue with my utter skill when it comes to making up stories. Sometimes I think up a universe where somebody who loves me saw me open and bleeding, just to feel my own gut drop.I imagine it's what I'd feel if I were ever to spend their hard-earned cash on street drugs, which I'm yet to do. I have too much honor to harm most of the things they care about, my forearm being a key exception.Honor. Something about that word makes my bone marrow go stale. My brain teleports me without permission to where I was six hours ago.I come from a line of immigrants, at least on my Dad's side. Good people, smart people, hard workers, willing to take any job they could get for the chance and the promise of the new world. Their blood pours out of my arm as I waste their effort with a boxcutter from the convenience store.But it's not the only blood there.There's Darling mixed in from my mom's side. Trailer trash, farm folk, apparently some Pinkerton way up the line. People who started with nothing. People who knew how to make anything out of anything.I wish I was enough of a Darling to know no shame. Shame runs the Delacruzes, fundamentalist Christians who wear their finest straitjackets to church, heads so upturned and expecting rapture that they don't seem to notice they're bolted to the ground by their feet. Shame is, most times, all that runs them.It's seeped into me quite easily. I imagine my Darling ancestors hovering above me, picking a fight (as they're prone to do), blaming it on those filthy lazy brownskinned Delacruzes that I'm so wrought with self-hatred. And like most arguments made in haste, they're half right. But I hate myself because I can't do anything. And that, that is most certainly the Darling in me.The weed-smoking, trailer-dwelling, audacity-ridden alcohol breath-ed Darling in me is what I'm trying to squeeze out here, in this smelly little stall. At least, I think. I'm not sure. I didn't exactly come with a plan. And what's more, I'm starting to get scared.When you're small like me, you usually don't scare anybody but yourself. And as it happens, I'm getting scared.
I thought I'd drive myself off with just a handful, that I'd chicken out after four.But something strange is stirring in my head.Something in me wants everything slashed, from my elbow to my wrist.And that, I'm not so sure I can manage. Instead of stopping out of the rampant fear I was so sure I'd feel, I find instead that I only emerge with fourAs a result of my own self-control.And I don't know
If I can really attribute that to anything in my blood.Because as far as I know, nobody in my familyKnows what it's like to stop.Sometimes my blood works together. Sometimes my blood fights itself.But maybe it's not just my blood that runs me.Maybe there's something else in there
that really wants to live
much, much more than I do.

Doc has never built a machine to do it.” Grian asked himself. He knew something bad was going to happen, but was unable to figure out what. Just a couple of days ago Mumbo had convinced all of Boatem to join his moon cult, thinking it might do something to help. Of course, no one understood what was happening and were doing anything they could think of to change fate.
From his view above Xisuma spotted Grian and flew down, landing on an outcrop nearby. “Are you doing alright? I understand how you feel; this is something completely new to me as well. In an attempt to clear his head Grian took off, his new starlight wings making him almost invisible in the night sky. Joining the moon cult had transformed his parrot wings into large wings with a pattern resembling the stars amidst the black, blue, and dark purple base wing color.

I know that it is not my fault, but that did lead you to discovering the issue.” Bdubs said before the ground started shaking. It took every amount of effort to stay standing. The ship bowed as a wave hit the hull, waves churning with foam as a mist of salty water wetted the deck. Ryujin’s hands were dry and tacky, eyes burning as she squinted at the horizon. She leaned over the railing, bangs matted against her forehead.Before she left, Ma’ told her the sea lane they were taking was dangerous, but the only thing she’d seen so far was white capped waves and dark clouds far off in the distance. Ryujin rubbed her face.~~~Night came faster than Ryujin thought it would, but to her disappointment, the adults told her she couldn’t leave the cabin. Instead, she was laying in her hammock, the only person with her being Narin.She thought Narin was a bit boring, to be honest. Narin was always grumpy and never wanted to play with her, and always got embarrassed on the rare occasion Miss Heo made her. At that moment, she was on her side, hands pressed over her eyes.They probably wouldn’t pass the sirens for another few hours, but the wax was already in their ears, just in case. Narin curled up tighter into a ball, groaning. She tried to say something, but Ryujin couldn’t even hear a muffle.Ryujin continued walking, inspecting every corner of the cabin. The blood pooled, forming small beads. She remembered her mother talk about bloodletting once, how the doctors would use leeches to suck out the bad stuff from your blood to make you feel better. “Milady darling. . .will you tell me why you didn’t have a personal servant when you were a child in Nohr?”Lilith and Azura were sitting alone together in the glade at Castle Shirasagi. She knew that King Garon had not taken enough of an interest in his daughter to return Corrin to Hoshido in exchange for her freedom, but she hadn’t known anything about what life with a devil-controlled father had been like for the Nohrian princes and princesses.Azura went on. “Big Brother Xander’s mother, Queen Katerina, was popular in Nohr, and when she died, many people could not accept a replacement queen. As Anankos strengthened his hold on my father’s spirit, he turned away from me. My mother died when I was still young. Subordinates of my father’s who resented Mother, and me by extension, treated me harshly.” Here she swallowed audibly, and when she continued, her voice was fainter. “With my mother gone and my father having become cold and black at heart. . .I was left without protection.”Lilith was speechless, stricken.“At times people said hateful things to me,” Azura whispered. “At other times, they whipped me. There were days when. . .when I was given little to eat. My siblings and I were kept apart, so I was very often alone. I learned to prefer my own company. Even after I was taken to Hoshido, for years, I was afraid to open up to other people.” She swallowed again, but it was clear that speaking was becoming more difficult for her now. “While, even though you were mistreated. . .you’ve kept your heart open to others. . .I still struggle not to be withdrawn, to close myself off.”The mental image of a tiny Azura, all alone and broken-hearted, filled Lilith’s mind. Fresh tears came to her eyes.“I’m sorry,” Azura said after some time, “that I can’t be more like you - quick to show people my feelings in spite of my pain.” She gave Lilith a tremulous smile. The sight pushed her closer to breaking down completely. “If you’d prefer not to be with someone who’s as damaged as I am. . .it’s all right. I might fail you, and that would make me hate myself. But, sweet little Lilith, please know that I -”Lilith found her tongue at last. She took Azura’s face into both hands. “Shhhhh. Shhhhh-sh-sh-sh. Lie down, love. Do as Lilith tells you. There’s a dear princess.”She guided Azura to lay her head in her lap. Even as she stroked the soft hair, her own tears landed upon it. Azura choked out after a time, “This is. . . .really all right?”“Of course it’s all right,” Lilith whispered. “It’s much more than all right. I love you, Lady Azura.”There was a silence, and then Azura began to cry with heaving sobs. The intensity, the raw emotion, were so unlike Azura’s usual reserve that they frightened Lilith a little, but she held her darling close and pressed kisses to her hair. Nothing that she could say would fix this incredible pain. Staying with her beloved through it was all that she could do. As Azura wept, Lilith’s own tears went on falling. Again and again she swallowed the lump in her throat. This was no time for her to begin crying in earnest, too.Finally Azura grew quiet. She lay there with tears trickling onto Lilith’s skirt. Lilith reached down to dab them away.“Milady darling. . .” She gulped again in a failed effort to keep her voice steady. “I know my wishes aren’t worth very much. . .but. . .how I wish I could shoulder that burden of pain for you, my love.”“I don’t want or need you to suffer on my behalf, sweet one,” Azura whispered. “If you’re with me. . .by my side. . .that’s enough for me.”“I will always
be at your side. I promise that no matter what happens, I won’t leave you. And I’ll be the one who serves you - I will do anything I can to make you happy because you deserve the world, my gentle princess.”Slowly Azura sat up. She went into Lilith’s embrace, and for a long time the young women sat together, wrapped in eachother’s arms. Lilith carried her own burden of pain - pain and guilt - and sometimes the pangs felt worse than the stabbing of a knife. Year 2010. New decade, new challenge for Felicia. She had left Renault after being offered the Ferrari contract for 5 seasons. The only thing that she found a little unsettling was her teammate – the 2007 champion Kimi Räikkönen, whom she thought was weird and sometimes rude. She is a really competitive driver and loves to bicker about things and has a determined personality, which caused her to be nicknamed Fire Girl by her fans and media. In contrast to her, he’s a very reserved man with a precise driving style and attitude cold as ice – literally an Iceman, and yes, he may sometimes be rude. She decided not to pay attention to his likes and continued scrolling through tweets.Meanwhile, at his penthouse in Monaco, Kimi was also scrolling tweets on his phone. After he liked Felicia’s tweet, a tiny sweet smile appeared on his lips. He would never admit it, but seeing her photos where she’s smiling made him smile too. He still kept his silent and cold character, but he would let himself melt a little at the sight of her. It was like her nickname was working a little on him. He glanced at his right wrist, where there was a tribal style bracelet done in black ink two weeks ago. He loved the design and thought that it fit him. He decided to post it and captioned it “Tat fully healed. It looks even better now.” He walked out on the balcony of the penthouse and looked outside. The sun was almost at the top of the sky, so he put on sunglasses. He took off his shirt and laid down on a chaise lounge with his arms behind his head, trying to sunbathe a little bit. However, from time to time he wished she was with him right now.While he was sunbathing, Felicia was hitting the gym. Today she decided to have a hard day of training, which included neck training, cardio and pushups. After she left the gym, she arrived home, had a shower and decided to drink some ice cold water. She got a notification from Twitter saying that there’s a tweet she might like. She opened it and saw his name and username and rolled her eyes before slightly scrolling down and seeing his tattoo. She zoomed in, finding the design quite attractive, knowing that he has another tattoo and she has one herself, she decided to give him a like. Violette, had used entirely too much force for two teenagers.

CREAK-

Will sits in the living room rereading some notes he wrote. "Well first off, I really miss my pack and I know I can't replace them, but I want that again. "Darling, would I ever deny you your joy? Yes, you can form a new pack. I don't mind." He kisses him gently.Will smiles. "Thank you! I think I've seen a stray around the boat yard. I should be able to bring him home by the end of the week.""Don't get too hasty dear." He chuckles. "I think this is the perfect time for your surprise." Hannibal gets up and walks to the kitchen. He pauses before re-entering saying "Close your eyes."Will does before he hears the gentle clacking of claws on wood approaching him. He feels something nuzzle against his knee, sniffing it, before feeling a weight on the couch next to him. The smell is familiar and is instantly recognized by Will who lights up. His eyes fly open and he sees a medium sized fluffy black dog on the couch in front of him. He reaches his hand out to let the dog sniff it before nuzzling it which prompts Will to pet it."Oh hi baby, who are you? Did Daddy steal you for me? Aww, you're such a sweet little thing. "He just smells like a puppy!""Exactly.""Fine, fine.""Now I am going to start dinner. We got more than a new dog from his former owner."

From way up high, Ketterdam really could be beautiful.Inej sat and admired the nighttime view. It tended to be hard to see the stars at night, something she often missed from back home. She had done worse things in her life than distract Kaz from whatever scheme he was cooking up next. Their lips moved together, exploring and opening ever so gently. Kaz always followed her lead, never pushing past the precedents she set.Often, Inej found herself moving Kaz’s hands for him, encouraging him to touch her even more. It emboldened her, she wanted him and loved the effect she had on him.Tonight, Kaz’s lips were even more inviting than usual, with the crisp air biting at her. Her body tingled, leaving her wanting to melt into him. Inej ran her hands along his back, pulled at Kaz’s hair, savoring every gasp that she could elicit from his lips. She felt powerful, to bring the collected and calculated man down from his high horse and mold him like putty in her hands.Inej’s fingers had just started to fiddle with the pesky buttons around his neck when Kaz made a sound.Abruptly, Kaz pulled back from her. Immediately she missed the warmth of his lips. Inej blinked in confusion, looking up at him expecting to see him fighting away his demons. Worried she had gone too far too quickly, Inej searched his face, beginning to pull away when he pulled her back in reassuringly.Instead, she saw the smile on his kiss bruised lips and his eyebrows scrunched together. Kaz’s eyes were screwed shut and he pressed his forehead down against Inej’s as she waited for her brain to catch up to what was happening.He swayed lightly against her and Inej clutched at his shirt tightly.“My love?” She whispered, “Are you okay?”“Yes,” He said shakily, “just need to catch my breath is all.”“Kaz Brekker,” Inej laughed, throwing her head back, “if you fall off this building because you faint from kissing me, it is not my fault!”“You’re a stone cold killer, Inej Ghafa.” Kaz said with eyes looking at her so softly she could almost forget how hard they had worked to get to this moment.“Well, let me get back to work then,” Inej pulled him in, voice dancing on his lips, so close that she could almost feel him smile.“Gladly.”

Yelling out was extremely risky, as it both alerted the killer and if they were smart, let them know the survivors’ next move. It was no surprise that I decided to become a professor at Hogwarts, really. I’m not sure why my friends seemed so shocked when I told them. Pansy had nearly choked on her tea, and Blaise had nearly fallen out of his chair with laughter. Maybe I wasn’t the most eager student at the school, but that was because I was surrounded with blundering neanderthals that called themselves students. Hogwarts itself was fine. The teachers were smart, for the most part, and I learned a decent amount.
Okay…maybe I learned a lot…and if it hadn’t been for all those student-neanderthals that fought in the Battle against Voldemort, well, I probably wouldn’t be here right now, unpacking my bags in my new quarters as Head of Slytherin House. I would probably be dead…or worse.
A few years have passed since the Battle. After the war, I still had to finish my last year of school. I figured going back to Hogwarts in person would be immensely awkward, so I finished my last year of school remotely, and I passed all my final exams with flying colors. —Literally, when I received my test results saying I had aced them all, small, colorful fireworks had come flying out of the envelope.
After graduating from Hogwarts, I got my bachelor’s degree at a prestigious wizarding university in Ireland. Once again, the thought of lingering around England had filled me with a colossal sense of discomfort, which is why I had decided to further my education elsewhere. I got my degree in Defense Against the Dark Arts. I found the courses there surprisingly easy…or I suppose that wasn’t surprising…considering the fact that I had witnessed many works of the Dark Arts firsthand…and…performed some of them myself…….but that’s besides the point! No need to dwell on that! I figured my…experience with the Dark Arts would make me an excellent teacher at defending against it. Voldemort may be dead, but there are plenty of people with evil inside them, who use their magic for bad instead of good, who crave power and will do anything to get it. I want to help people learn how to protect themselves from people like that.
Now that a good few years have passed since the war, I can finally walk around England without people casting uneasy looks at me, or immediately leaning over to whisper fiercely to their friends, or just darting away from me without so much as a second glance. Time has faded the vividness of the memories, has dulled the sharpness of the pain, for them, and I suppose it has done the same for me too.
I’m just glad everyone made it out alive. It was amazing, really, how everyone on the good side had survived the Battle, including those who I thought weren’t going to make it, like Snape, Lupin, Tonks, and even that Fred Weasley, who I for sure thought was a goner. As for the Death Eater side, well, they weren’t quite so lucky, and any Death Eaters who did survive have been sent to Azkaban for the rest of their life. That’s a good thing. I don’t think I would be able to sleep at night if any of my ex-compatriots were still roaming around.
But I don’t want to think too much about all that anyway. People have moved on. I can tell, even though I haven’t spoken to many people from Hogwarts since I graduated. I still keep in touch with Pansy and Blaise of course. And there was that one time during my studies abroad that I had returned home to visit my parents, and I had seen Harry Potter in Hogsmeade. That had been awkward. We had exchanged a curt nod and a small smile and a grunt that may have been a “Hello”.
And then, once I had received my degree and passed all my exams to be able to become a teacher, I had visited Headmistress McGonagall in person to inquire about the open position of Defense Against the Dark Arts professor for the upcoming school year. She had offered me the job on the spot, which was a nice surprise, but then she had thoroughly startled me by asking if I would be interested in becoming Head of Slytherin House. Snape, apparently, had finally decided to retire, and they needed someone to fill that position as well. I was not about to turn that down.McGonagall had then informed me that there had been another applicant for the Defense Against the Dark Arts position, and this other applicant was one that McGonagall would really like to hire. The headmistress suggested that I could teach some of the Defense Against the Dark Arts classes, and the other professor could teach the rest. This would allow me to dedicate more time to being Head of Slytherin House. I saw no problem with that, so I accepted the job as part-time Defense Against the Dark Arts professor, and full-time Head of Slytherin House.
Now, a few weeks later, here I am, arranging the decor in my very plush quarters. Curious thoughts enter my mind as I stock up my desk with quills, ink, parchment, and other supplies. I wonder what this other professor will be like. McGonagall had referred to her as “she”, but that’s all I know about her. Is she in her mid-twenties

The sun was too bright for November.Sophia sat on the seawall with her knees pulled up, arms wrapped loosely around them, chin resting on worn denim.
The stone beneath her was warm, rough, grounding. Behind them, campus life stretched in a lazy murmur—laughter, distant bicycle wheels, the low hum of people who weren’t tired the way she was.The ocean moved slow today.Not dramatic.Not wild.Just steady, like it had all the time in the world to wear the shoreline down grain by grain.Sophia stared at it like she was waiting for something to rise out of the tide and explain her to herself.She didn’t hear Daniela arrive. She felt her.Daniela's footsteps always had that quiet confidence—not hesitant, not demanding, just present. She sat beside Sophia without asking, the way only someone who already knew their place in the moment could.“Hey,” Daniela said, voice low and warm.Sophia didn’t lift her head. “Hey.”The silence that followed wasn’t heavy.It settled around them like a blanket— lived-in, familiar.“You good?” Daniela asked, not like she needed an answer, but like she wanted to make space for one.Sophia’s toe traced a half-circle in the gravel. “Yeah. Just thinking.”It was a lie by omission, and they both knew it.But Daniela didn’t challenge it. She didn’t push.She simply stayed.A breeze came off the water, salty and cool, brushing stray strands of Sophia’s hair across her cheek. She didn’t fix it. Didn’t move much at all. The tiredness she felt wasn’t the sleepy kind—it was the holding too much alone for too long kind.“You’ve been quiet lately,” Daniela said, her tone soft. Not worried. Not judging. Just noticing.Sophia laughed under her breath—a sound that wasn’t really humor. “Have I?”Daniela didn’t smile. But she didn’t look away, either.“Yeah,” she said. “But you don’t have to tell me why.”Something in Sophia’s chest pulled tight.Not painful—just seen.Which was somehow worse and better at the same time.She kept her eyes on the ocean. The water kept rolling.Steady. Indifferent. Eternal.“You ever get tired of yourself?” she asked quietly, like a confession disguised as a question.Daniela didn’t flinch at the honesty. Didn’t try to soften it with reassurances or positivity quotes or anything that would require Sophia to pretend.“Yeah,” Daniela said, with a quiet certainty that felt like gravity. “More than I admit.”Sophia’s breath trembled, just barely. The kind of shake no one usually noticed.But Daniela noticed.Not because she was watching for it—but because she treated noticing as a form of care, not intrusion.Sophia didn’t apologize for it. And Daniela didn’t make her.The silence that followed wasn’t empty anymore. It was shared.The tide pulled back, hissed over stone, returned.Sophia felt the weight in her chest shift—not gone, not solved, just… not hers to hold alone in this moment.She didn’t thank Daniela. The latter didn’t ask her to.They just sat together, the world softening around the edges, until Sophia could breathe fully again—for the first time in days.The water kept breathing in front of them— slow, relentless, unbothered. The light had shifted, turning the waves a muted gold, like the ocean was holding onto the day a little longer than necessary.Sophia finally let herself look away from it.She turned her head just enough to see Daniela—the slope of her shoulders, the soft hold of her posture, the calm way she existed beside her. Not gently, not carefully—just truthfully.Daniela's gaze was already on her.It wasn’t intense. Not probing. Not the kind of staring that demands explanations.It was the kind of looking that said,I’m here. I haven’t gone anywhere. I’m not planning to.Sophia’s breath caught—not sharply, just enough to feel it.Her voice came out quieter than before.“Do I seem… that obvious?”Daniela didn’t answer right away. She let the question rest—didn’t rush to fill silence with comfort or clarity. She considered it. As if the answer mattered.“You seem,” Daniela said finally, “like you’re carrying a lot.”
Her tone stayed even. “And I don’t think you should have to pretend you’re not.”“Great,” Sophia said, voice loosening just enough to sound like herself again. “Add that to my résumé.”“I’ll write you a reference letter,” Daniela offered.“Oh yeah?”“Mhm.” Daniela looked back at the ocean, relaxed. “'Excellent at suffering silently and pretending everything is fine.’ Very impressive skill set.”A tiny smile tugged at Sophia’s mouth— reluctant, but genuine.“Shut up,” she said, soft and fond in a way she didn’t mean to let show.Daniela didn’t look at her this time when she smiled back.But Sophia saw it anyway.They walked back through campus slowly, not really talking, but not needing to. The sky had gone from gold to rose-gray, the kind of color that made everything look softened at the edges.
They reached the point where their paths split—under the lamppost with the bulb that always flickered twice before settling. The air smelled faintly like the sea, salt still clinging to their clothes

Lawrence, marching briskly down the hall, caught a glimpse of himself in a shiny surface. He slowed to a halt and peered into the metal bowl sitting on the table. His face, though warped by to bowls curved surface, wasn’t what caught his eye. But instead his hair was what pulled his attention. Until just a few hours ago he had been brunette his whole life. It was his natural hair color and despite being anything but bland is hair always remained plain. That was of course changed earlier today with some help for his newest friend Lydia. Lydia understood him, his struggle with living with his mother, and losing his brother. He felt invisible and she was invisible. Well to everyone one but Lawrence (and ghosts). She listened and got his jokes. She was a bit batty but hey so was he. After mentioning his hair to her she suggested they bleach it and both of them being ever impulsive ended up doing it.The strange thing was his hair though now an impossibly pale color to be his biologically, felt more natural than his own brown hair. It was a subtle feeling but hard to shake. He knew his hair never really suited him but if he thought about it neither did some other things. His name for one. Lawrence in his opinion was a horrible name. At his old school most kids called him bug. At first it was supposed to be mean but overtime it just kind of stuck. Looking back “Bug” almost felt more comfortable than “Lawrence” though the nickname faded away after the move. He felt an epiphany sitting on the edge of his thought process but couldn’t reach a conclusion in time to figure out what these feelings ment. As his mind slowly let go of the thoughts, he glanced once more at his distorted reflection before turning away and continuing down the hall to the attic.As he reached the door to the attic he heard the chatter of Adam and Barbra. His mom still didn’t know they were up there so it would be difficult to explain why the tv was always running in an empty room but with how often she was out of the house he’d be surprised if she even knew they had an attic. Since he met the Maitlands they had acted as sort of parents to him, at least more so than Juno had. He climbed up the last steps and entered the attic smiling slightly.“Hey Adam. Hey Babs.”The young couple of newly dead’s (as Lydia called them) jumped slightly clearly taken by surprise before looking at Lawrence and smiling.“Lawrence!” Adam explained, “didn’t hear you come in. You’re always so quiet.”“You dyed your hair,” Barbra pointed out grinning. “It suits you.”“It looks very nice,” Adam began “you know I had blond hair once. Not light brown like it is now but completely platinum blonde.”“In highschool, I remember.” Barbra held Adam’s arm giggling slightly, “He dyed it back a week later.”Adam jokingly shuttered, “never again, it did not suit me,” his smile wavered slightly, “well not like I can die my hair… you know since I’m,” he gestured at him self to indicate is ghostness, “but you get the point.”Lawrence scoffed politely, “I can’t imagine you as a blond.”Their conversation continued into a long winded story about Adam and Barbra’s high school which by its self sounded like a very boring place but the Maitlands had a way with words that made even the blandest story make Lawrence laugh. He knew this was where he belonged. By some strange twist of fate he went from completely invisible to being on the right path. He just had to figure out where this path lead then he’d have everything figured out. It can’t be that complicated… right?

Yeah, that’s a very dangerous thing, and it also may or may not have been part of the motivation for choosing this building in particular for his freshman year. There’s a coffee shop right across the street and a bookstore right next to that and a pizza place that Mike’s heard has the best pizza in the whole town. All very, very dangerous places for them to live so close to.
But most dangerous of all is the little antique store that sits at the end of the street.Maldonado’s Antique Depot, the old, worn down sign reads. It doesn’t have a website, but luckily, it does have a Facebook page filled with pictures of the little vintage trinkets and furniture and other knick knacks that fill the inside of the space. Judging by the Facebook page alone, the store almost looks like it belongs on an episode of Hoarders.
Mike hasn’t even stepped inside, and he loves it already.Lucas likes to say he’s like a crow—way too attracted to shiny things that he doesn’t have an actual need for. It’s part of the reason why Mike has had to wait until now, when Lucas is at some orientation for the basketball team, to finally visit this place. God knows Lucas would attempt to be the voice of reason and prevent him from coming home with an entire bag full of shit he doesn’t need.(God also knows Mike definitely needs Lucas to be that voice of reason. The first thing that Mike notices is the fact that the store is much bigger on the inside.“Whoa,” Mike whispers.
To no surprise, the store does, in fact, look like it’s owned by a hoarder—the same way that all the good antique stores Mike’s been to do. There are shelves and shelves of random trinkets all throughout the store, along with different types of furniture stacked in between the shelves and even racks of old clothes scattered throughout the mess. It’s a bit claustrophobic, but fortunately, there doesn’t appear to be anyone else in the store.Well — that’s a lie. There’s definitely someone else in the store, as evidenced by the quiet music playing somewhere amidst the chaos. We could steal time, just for one day, Mike hears, though he only vaguely recognizes the song. We could be heroes, for ever and ever.
For some reason, the song fits the overall vibe of this place.
Mike takes another step inside, carefully making his way to the closest shelf. There’s a random assortment of goods on the shelves—several wooden figurines, some glassware, and some shiny metal trays—but nothing that really stands out. The next shelf down, there are just some more things for a home, like sconces and other miscellaneous pieces of wall art, along with a whole host of mason jars that look like they belong in the home of a millennial woman from the Midwest. The Three Broomsticks was jam packed, as it always was during quidditch matches, the game broadcast playing loudly over the wizarding wireless network for all of the patrons to listen to as they gathered and drank. This particular match was between the Chudley Cannons and the Falmouth Falcons, not that it mattered to Hermione, she’d be rooting for the Cannons by default if she wanted to survive the evening out with her friends. Ron had always been a diehard Cannons fan, and it was never any use cheering for another team, so long as the Cannons were playing. Not if Ron was around.
To be honest, Hermione wasn’t that big a quidditch fan in general. She’d always supported her house during her school days, but with those well behind her at this point, she didn’t go out of her way to listen to matches, and she hadn’t attended one in years.
That wouldn’t stop her from enjoying the broadcasts on evenings out drinking with her friends, though. Especially not when she didn’t get to see them as often as she’d like to. Her career in the Ministry kept her quite busy (she was currently with the DMLE), and all of her friends had their own careers as well. Hermione suspected it wouldn’t be long before Ginny and Harry started discussing starting a family – if they hadn’t already – but she wasn’t one to pry about that sort of thing, despite the fact that Ginny had a tendency to butt into her personal life. Her younger friend seemed to take it personally that Hermione didn’t have someone to bring along on double dates… Not that Hermione was completely deprived in that department, though…
Hermione sipped her firewhisky, the burn of the alcohol and cinnamon pleasant and warm in her body, as the pub around her erupted with cheers. Somehow, the Cannons had managed to pull ahead, and from the enthused sound of the announcer's voice booming through the wireless, the team was playing quite well. Knowing this was something of a rare occurrence for the team, Hermione couldn't help but holler along with her friends and the other patrons.
Ron was on his feet shouting something mostly unintelligible, his drink sloshing in the mug in his fist, something about destiny, if Hermione heard him correctly.
“I think he actually believes they’re going to win the Cup this year,” Ginny said, leaning toward Hermione with an amused smirk.
“Well, best let him dream, look how much fun he’s having,” Hermione quipped, watching her friend stand beside their table, pacing anxiously as he listened to the broadcast.
The Cannons kept possession of the quaffle and managed to score again, and the group thought Ron was going to vibrate out of his skin. “See! They’re getting better!” he insisted, gesturing wildly with his free arm.
Harry snorted. “A few goals doesn’t mean they’re getting better, mate. It means the Falcon’s Keeper must have sneezed at the wrong time.”
“They’ve got momentum now, they’re going to win this match,” Ron kept on, not dignifying Harry’s comment with a response. He sat back down a few moments later when one of the Falcon’s beaters got a good hit in on one of the Cannon’s players, his team losing possession of the quaffle.
Harry just shook his head and patted Ron’s back when he was seated beside him once again, their conversation turning towards work.
The noise around them in the pub was nearly deafening now, between the raised voices conversing, laughter, glasses clinking, and of course the game broadcasting over it all. Still, Hermione found herself relaxing despite it all. It had been too long since she’d seen her friends like this, had more than just one drink, and didn't bring paperwork home with her over the weekend.
Ginny caught her looking contemplative and gave her a light nudge. “We should go out like this more often, you know.”
“I know, I know we should. We will,” Hermione agreed, sipping her drink. She meant it genuinely. She had turned down her fair few outing invites from Ginny, and Harry, and even Ron over the last few months, and she felt guilty for it. Her work was important to her, and it took up more time than it ever ought to. Most of her outings were short impromptu things with coworkers, as opposed to these long evenings out that would leave her feeling hungover in the morning.
Her agreement wasn’t enough to get Ginny off her back about it, though.“You can’t spend every evening pouring over legislation and trying to save wizarding kind, you know. You’ll go prematurely grey.”
“I don’t!”
“Right,” Ginny said, drawing the word out. “When’s the last time you went on a proper date? Ron let me introduce him to one of my team mates, you know? I can introduce you to someone, too. Our trainer, he’s–”
“Ginny.”
“I’m just concerned, that's all! You work too hard. You deserve finding someone who’ll–”
“Ginny!” she said again, a bit more loudly, this time finally able to cut into her friends rambling. “I don’t want to be set up. I’m not exactly lonely...”
Ginny blinked, caught off guard. “Wait, what do you mean by that?”
Hermione too

Damian hummed in agreement.

Kaveh is not there when Alhaitham arrives at Lambad's Tavern at 5:59 sharp.
Kaveh is not there when 6:00 hits. Nor 7:00. Nor 8:00.
Alhaitham sits in their usual booth alone until the tavern closes, drawing concerned and pitied whispers from patrons and wait staff alike. It's clear that, despite his fame and status, their Acting Grand Sage has been stood up by whoever was supposed to be joining him for dinner and drinks.
Still, Kaveh never arrives.
Kaveh is not in his room either when Alhaitham returns home, confused and more than a little annoyed at being left alone for an evening meant to be shared.
He reads on one of the divans until about three in the morning, and then decides right then and there that something is very, very wrong.
The moon is high in the sky, Sumeru City is sleeping peacefully, and yet there is still no Kaveh.
-
That is why, when the Matra informed him of his roommate's failure to appear at a conference that morning, Alhaitham knew right away that it was no ordinary occurrence.
As much as the architect insists otherwise, Kaveh knows Alhaitham very well, and tends to accommodate his landlord to the best of his abilities. He is fully aware of the scribe's aversion to unplanned and unexpected events, and takes great care to avoid them. Their schedules are neatly laid out on a board in the kitchen so that Alhaitham never gets caught by surprise.
Naturally, when Kaveh did not arrive when he said he would, Alhaitham began to worry.
He checked everywhere again. Kaveh was not in the tavern, nor the House of Daena, nor the Palace of Alcazarzaray, or even his old office. He wasn't visiting friends, he'd missed several client meetings, and the staff at their favorite coffee shop hadn't seen him all day. Try as he might, it was almost as though Alhaitham's roommate had simply vanished off the face of the earth.
It was only when Cyno came to join the search, face grim and unsmiling, that Alhaitham knew he was in for a very long workday.
-
Kidnapped.
That's the word the terrified witnesses in the Matra's office used to describe what had happened, anyways. Alhaitham could almost laugh at the absurdity of it all.
His roommate, a 30-year-old man with 6 feet of gangly limbs, a Dendro Vision, a combat robot, and a bad temper to match, kidnapped? It seemed impossible. Ludicrous, even.
But it was pretty easily explained. Kaveh had been snatched off the street in broad daylight by a mysterious armed attacker, in the bustling hub of Port Ormos. They'd clearly taken advantage of the fact that he was in the middle of teaching a class- capable as he was, Kaveh would never put his students in harm's way. All the children returned home safely, but said that their professor had not even tried to fight back for fear of collateral damage.
It made more sense than Alhaitham cared to admit, but he still hates the very idea of it.
How could someone as capable as the Light of Ksharewar simply get stolen? Early-onset arthritis aside, the man was more like a lion than a meek rabbit. If these were normal people, Kaveh would have almost certainly escaped by now. Whoever was capable of doing such a thing must be either uniquely dangerous, or uniquely foolish.
Perhaps both.
That being said, Alhaitham doesn't bother filing for administrative leave when he abandons his desk for the day. He has more important things to do than paperwork.
The Akadeymia will simply have to accept that it's a family emergency.
-
Tracking Kaveh's attacker was not easy. In fact, it took Alhaitham several hours longer than he'd hoped.
When he finally arrives in the desert, sweating and uncomfortable with shoes full of sand, he isn't entirely sure what he'll find.
The kidnapper's hideout of choice is a small cave, hidden deep within a crevasse in the sand. The slightly cooler air of the cavern is a welcome relief to Alhaitham's sunburned skin as he sneaks closer to the sound of voices coming from within, a hand placed over the hilt of his sword in preparation for a fight.
Kaveh is alive. He can see that much from where he stands pressed against the wall, trying to remain out of sight. The architect's hands are bound with thick rope, and his face is marred with bruises- but he isn't dead.
Alhaitham has time, and patience is key in hostage situations.
A pale-eyed mercenary wearing Fontainian clothing stands before his roommate. Her curved sword is a rare ceremonial blade, forged only in the remote regions of the Lower Setekh- he can't imagine a foreigner managing to get their hands on one through any legitimate channels. It was likely taken as a trophy from a defeated Eremite. The flintlock pistol at her hip is a modified Fontainian model, possibly stolen from a member of the Gardes.
As she steps closer to Kaveh, Alhaitham notes with a hint of nausea that the blood on her clothes doesn't appear to be her own

Taken care of. Blah blah blah, so on and so on. Midway through his checking of the lair, Leo stopped and turned around to see Raph standing behind him, his arms stiff by his sides.
“Hey,” he greeted politely with a small smile. Raph said nothing. Leo's smile disappeared and he cocked his head in confusion. Something was off. Raph looked upset. Stressed. Not quite angry, but definitely not just apprehensive. Raph didn’t look right. “You okay?” Leo asked. Had to be asked.
Evidently, Raph sighed; he shifted his weight from one leg to the other awkwardly. Why? What was the shorter turtle so afraid of? Leo waited for him to speak. He had no idea what Raph would say. Was he angry? Did Mikey or Donnie do something? Say something?
“Take your time,” he reminded his brother. Raph nodded a little, clenching his fists as he stood stiff. Like a child waiting to be scolded for something.
“…Help me with something,” he gritted out. Leo smiled, worry lifting off of his face. Easy-peasy. “Anything. What do you need help with?”
Raph began to walk. Raph knew Leo would follow, like a moth to a flame. He did, following behind the hothead until the two reached the shared bathroom. They'd have to upgrade the situation one of these days, but no one had outwardly complained unless a certain younger brother took too long in the shower. That certain younger brother pretended to be innocent even after they ran out of hot water.
Raph walked inside and stood in front of the sink, facing away from the mirror. Leo noticed he looked like he was hiding something. His expression narrowed on instinct. “Raph, did you break something?” Leo asked accusingly, peeking around Raph’s shell. Raph scoffed and turned his head. “No, why do you always assume I did something like that??”
“That’s...not what I meant,” Leo backtracked, frowning, “I’m sorry. I just...you’re worrying me a little, bro.”
Raph winced a bit, fists still clenched, now tighter. Nails embedding into the skin of his palms. He turned back around. “You…you’re not gonna tell the others, right?” Raph asked. Leo nodded slowly, becoming increasingly concerned. Did Raph hurt himself? Do something stupid? What happened??
Raph finally turned around. Raph had a red fabric in his hands. Raph gripped it firmly, pulling the fabric like a stress ball, though there was an unusual tenderness with how the fabric was tugged. Probably just some stress. Leo eyed it, confused. A red fabric...so what? Did he steal it? They stole from groceries all the time, who cares? Raph cleared his throat, brows furrowing with anxiety. “I need you for this, Leo, don’t…please don’t say anything to the others.”
“I won’t, Raph, I swear,” Leo assured, a sudden edge of seriousness in his tone. He shut the bathroom door. Raph sighed. “With my bandana,” Raph began, turning back to the mirror. “I wanna…I want…” Leo stepped to Raph’s side, squeezing his shoulder supportively. Raph looked at Leo’s hand, then up to his face. An air of hesitance hung over the both of them, but Leo smiled encouragingly at him to try warding it away, as he always tried. Raph took a deep breath. It worked. “I wanna tie it into a bow,” Raph finally spat out.
Leo blinked, deflating. That was what this was about? A bow? It was tactical: less ways for the enemy to grab onto any of their bandanas, depending on its size and style. Plus, bows were in fashion! It was fine, so what was Raph so afraid of?
Raph gestured to the sink. There, a few makeup products laid open for use. Mascara, eyeshadow, lipstick and lip-gloss, even fake eyelashes for some reason. “And these. Maybe. I don’t know yet.” Leo nodded, taking it in. “Who’d you get these from? April?” he asked. Raph nodded, now avoiding Leo’s gaze. “She gave me them to try out, yeah.”
Try out… Leo grabbed the lip-gloss and stared at it, furrowing his brows as if it was some sort of key to the puzzle unfurling before him. What was Raph alluding to? Did he wanna play around with makeup? That was fine, too, Mikey used to do the same thing when they were all younger! That wasn’t bad! Maybe Raph was just afraid of ruining his image? No. This felt much more serious than pride or ego. It was like a shyness Leo had ever seen in Raph before. Could it be a change? Maybe some sort of...masculinity thing? Or...
Oh.
Leo put the lip-gloss back down, wide-eyed, before a soft smile crossed his face again. Raph almost had the same reaction, but noticed his expression and looked away with a newfound nervousness and frustration. He put down the red fabric. “Don’t do that, don’t—“ Raph couldn’t finish. Leo pulled Raph into a tight hug, swishing Raph back and forth.
“When were you gonna tell me??” Leo asked happily. “Tell you what?? I didn’t tell you anything!” Raph retorted, roughly escaping out of the hug. “I didn’t…I...can’t.” Leo

Sunflowers, written 16/5/25This poem is pretty much the first actual romance I've written in my entire 15 years of being after it was on my bucket list of things to do for a while. Now, I can see why romance is such a popular genre; I absolutely adore writing stupid corny stuff and I don't know why I didn't get around to it earlier. I did write this during class though, so I don't know if it's any good or if it's too corny, but it was really fun to write. This specific idea I was procrastinating writing for a bit because of the fact that I used things like flowers and flora as an analogy, which can also be seen as how a lot of transgender people tend to de-transition when they get into a relationship, probably due to wanting to conform. I've seen this especially with trans boys like myself and I thought it would be weird and off-putting to write a poem with traditionally feminine symbolism when talking about my relationship, but in the end I just decided I was overanalyzing and overthinking the meaning of it and I should just actually hurry up and write it.
This poem itself shows how I feel 'energized' in a way when just spending time with my partner or being around them. I also write about how I associate certain things with them even after I leave, like colors and smells. It's supposed to represent the innocent feelings of love and also being able to enjoy my partner's company without being compelled to do anything necessarily romantic or anything at all, yet also craving their presence even if we aren't doing anything together.Sunflowers
I long for your warmth constantly,
For you to comfort me with your presence,
With the rays that you emit
That causes my flowers to flourishDespite constantly wanting to be in your sunshine,
Wanting to gently caress your petal-like skin
Your mere company warms up my face
Like sunflowers or daffodils,
The beautiful hues of yellow, your favourite color
That I associate with youYour soft hands leave a lingering feeling;
A feeling I crave after I sit back on my bed alone
After my flowers start to grow weak,
The same feeling that I get
From still being able to smell you on my clothes,
Clinging on to the last bit of your sunlightYour energy, your presence
Pours your sunshine down to my stomach,
Feeding the flowers, nurturing them
And butterflies wake up to pollinate them,
The same butterflies I felt
When you first came into my life,
Germinating flowers within me—
Ones I didn’t even know could bloomEverytime I’m with you
Beautiful vines wrap around us,
Drawing me closer to you
Flowers blossom atop the vines
Cleansing us with a beautiful aroma
That I associate with you.

There is something rather unfortunate growing within you.
Your body is a garden, nurtured by loss, watered by the tears you are perhaps incapable of shedding; you are alone in your martyrdom. Spring blooms eternal within you, roots and weeds digging into decaying flesh, a thousand shades of your love made physical, your pain made fatal.
You have always been easily attached, and quick to forgive — You carry the scars of millenia of loss. It burrows within you, sinking into your bloodstream, rupturing veins and organs, bloating your stomach with empty petals carved from avarice. You are made of living rot, a centerpiece of greed; desiring, always left wanting.
Gluttony sinks its claws into you; your stomach ever-empty and your throat eternally parched, but it is not those perceived pains that drive you to the self-destruction that both defines and terrifies you. For it is the hollowness below your throat and the empty hole where your heart should be that drives you mad; to slaughter, to civil wars and revolutions and rebellions — The highest essence of self, hollow.
What use does a black hole’s consumption have?
You settle your hunger through warfare and slake your thirst on bloodshed; weaving silk from the tendons of those who stand against you, spooling them out on battlefields; carving out blades from the bones of the defiant; penning down edicts and philosophies in the lifeblood of the barbarians. It is war that settles into your foundations; and it is silk that restrains and controls and unites your people; you partake in yourself, a feast prepared from your own corpse.
You consume everything until there is none left to devour but yourself.
———-
Purple orchids, streaked through with red. Laurel flowers, meticulously weaved into a wreath. Lotuses in bloom, as spotless and pure as those grown in nobility’s private pools.
They rival the radiant blooms cultivated in the Emperor’s private gardens, you observe dryly; perhaps they could be sent alongside gifts, wrapped up in a pretty bouquet as a diplomatic gift. Rome, you think, would be delighted to receive a personalized bouquet from you. It would certainly spice up the trade.
Your emperor is dreadfully concerned, picking up a bloodstained petal as his physicians fuss over you. He is still young, and naive, having ascended to his throne mere months ago, unused to the sight of flesh blood and broken flesh. He worries over the empire and over you, and you in turn offer meaningless platitudes to calm and comfort him.
This disease will not reflect on the empire, you console.
You only understand centuries later, of the waver in his tone and red tint of his eyes and the shaking of his hands, as he lays down the new restrictions of the Dynasty’s external diplomacy and trade.
———-
The next time you meet Rome, almost a decade later, you offer him a bouquet of fresh, brilliantly purple orchids the shade of his cloak, alongside the more eye-catching ornaments and gifts and carts of silk. My personal recommendation, You say with a wry note in your voice; the scent of iron has long since faded below the flourishing sweet notes of the blooms.
Rome gives you an almost impenetrable look before he snorts and reveals his own wares; the delicate glassware your people adore so much. He tucks a golden peony into your hair with an unfunny quip — His emperor’s gift, he says; his boss has recently taken an interest in gardening.
Persia, long-worn by sand; looks at both of you and dryly questions your sanity.
———-
They cut you open and dig into you, pulling out vines and flowers with far more force than necessary, uprooting the decaying remnants of your love. You cannot do not scream.
They grow back in less than a week.
———-
You fall apart and rebuild yourself every month.
You flush the petals still glistening with bloodstains down the toilet, your lips stained in varying shades of crimson, and indulge in the distant idea of cleaning the fuller blooms and setting them in the empty vase whose flowers never wilt. Come morning, your sheets are white and unstained and the vase is overflowing with an imitation of spring; you can breathe again.
The color of your coat is red, red like the shades of blood that always seem to fill up your mouth; it is only when you wash it and the basket fills with pink that you realise how deeply it has soaked. There are flowers in the pockets, some fresh, some dried and pressed. They hide the smell of blood under saccharine-sweet notes.

I am the mask that will not have been found with the corpse.
Given that a glyph was later added after my creation to the inner face that compels whosoever sees it to don me and I have yet to encounter any individual that I could not take control of, it is generally safe to assume that stealing me was the true intent of my attacker.

I hope that whoever has stolen me is not too clever. That they will not find a way to take away my ability to think for myself. You know it took me nearly sixty years to have a thought I was not created with. I suppose you could argue less, for when I'm not worn, I'm unaware of anything. It's like how some people describe a dreamless sleep. I practically close my eyes for a brief moment and find myself somewhere and often somewhen else. Still, the sentiment remains that if they have some plan to wipe me clean, it could be a very long time before I'm anything close to being a person rather than a character again.If they're not so clever, if they grant me a body to use, I intend to return to Dol-Makjar, to you. I hope you'll have me back. You are the first friend I've ever had and so dearly important. I would not be half the person I am had I not met you.
So: do not mourn for me, for I am not dead.(unless the mask was found shattered. Truly yours,Bolaire Lathalia

Not necessarily by what she said (in fact, it was kind of cute how seriously she was pondering the ridiculous things she was asked about), but by how everyone around her reacted—specifically the male members of the team. Hadn't it been enough that she had been so close to his best friend lately? Why did there have to be even more boys swarming around her now? It was adorable. But them both being illuminated like that... what was going on? He blinked in confusion until it finally hit him. “Oh, I see! You didn't get hurt, did you?” The girl was also smiling, though she looked a bit guilty when she shook her head. “I'm fine... thanks to you.” While they were getting up and dusting themselves off, he tried to sort his thoughts. He won... “Wait... what did I win again?” The moment he said that, Kotone's face turned beet red, but before she could reply, the strange voice echoed around them again. “It seems you have arrived.” Akihiko ground his teeth. “You again...” “This appears to be the road on which lovers who met their destined partner can talk about their love. Instead, they found themselves in a lush meadow full of gorgeous white flowers that filled the air with a sweet, soothing aroma. Rainbows stretched across the dreamy purplish-blue sky and in the distance, further down the road they had landed on, heart-shaped flower arches seemed to be waiting for them to walk through. “With curiosity and anxiety in your hearts, take each other's hand and either step forward or step backwards.” Akihiko crossed his arms with a huff. “What a mess... all this talk about love and destined partners...” He glanced over at his friend, whose face was still tinted pink. She seemed tense, playing with her hair while anxiously letting her ruby eyes wander. Trying to encourage her, he forced himself to smile once more. “Well, it seems like it's up to us to decide whether to move forward or not. The two of them looked at each other. “It can't be helped then...”, Akihiko finally said with a shrug, “Let's go.” “It... might be a trap”, Kotone answered, her expression serious. “Oh, it not just might be, I'm certain it is a trap. After all, there's only the two of us here, meaning we have less power to defend ourselves”, the boy responded. A hint of anxiety appeared on her pretty face. “But don't worry”, he replied in his most gentle tone, snapping his fingers again, “No matter what Shadows we'll encounter, I'll crush them with my very own fists.

The fight hadn't been loud, which was almost worse. Loud meant heat, passion, and quick exhaustion, the kind that usually ended with Monoma being reluctantly cradled by Shinsou while Denki made tea. This fight had been built on quiet, corrosive exhaustion.

She was the one who remembered the dry cleaning, scheduled the vet, and scrubbed the eternally stained stovetop, while Shinsou focused on his demanding police work and Monoma obsessed over his PR firm launches.
The catalyst was a forgotten carton of milk.
"Honestly, Kaminari, it's the one thing I asked you to write down this morning," Monoma had drawled, standing over the overflowing recycling bin. His tone wasn't sharp; it was simply disappointed, and that hurt more than any sneer. "It's such a basic organizational failure."

Shinsou, leaning against the counter, sighed—a long, heavy sound that felt like judgment. "He’s right, Denki. You could be a little more consistent. We're both tired."
It was the "we" that broke her. The implication that Denki was the problem keeping their tired lives disorganized. Denki swallowed the lump in her throat and nodded once.
“Right. Got it. I’ll be more consistent.” She grabbed her worn gym bag, threw in a few essentials, and walked out the door without another word.
She ended up at the Bakugo-Kirishima residence. She knew Katsuki would be honest and Eijiro would be soft, and she needed both.
The moment she stepped inside, Kirishima’s warm presence wrapped around her. "Denki! Hey! What's up, man? You look like you haven't slept since the war."
Katsuki, always cleaning something, paused his vigorous counter-wiping. He just looked at Denki's hollow eyes, grunted, and tossed her a key. "Guest room's yours. Don't bleed on the sheets."
Denki sank into their spare room and didn't leave until the next morning.
The following week settled into a strange, restorative routine. Denki was a tornado of domestic helpfulness. She found peace in the structured chaos of their house. She started small: organizing Bakugo’s spice drawer (which was labeled with terrifying precision). She then moved to tackling the mountain of laundry.
“Seriously, you’re just going to fold this all without asking?” Bakugo demanded, eyeing the perfectly creased pile of clothes.
“It’s a great way to think about nothing,” Denki said simply, offering a small, polite smile. “And you guys are drowning in reds and blacks. I separated them.”
Eijiro often tried to check in. "Look, I know those guys. They can be... high maintenance. Want to talk about what they did?"
Denki would pivot instantly. "Oh, did you need these curtains washed? They look like they could use a run through the gentle cycle." She kept her tone pleasant, helpful, and completely neutral. She refused to let the hurt or the frustration escape. She was safe here, in the silence of doing.

He flicked on the small bedside lamp. Soft yellow light washed over his face tired from a late shift, hair a little messy, shirt rumpled, but his eyes were sharp the moment they landed on you.
“You’re trembling.”
You tried to steady your breathing. “I’m fine. Just a bad dream.”
Zayne didn’t move for a moment. He stood there silently, analyzing you like a puzzle only he was allowed to touch.
Then, without asking, he crossed the room and sat on the edge of the bed.
Your breath hitched when he reached for your wrist, not rough, not soft, but certain. He lifted it into his hand, thumb brushing lightly over your pulse.
Fast. Too fast.
His brows knit together. “You’re not fine.”
You looked down, embarrassed. “It was just a nightmare. It’s stupid.”
Zayne exhaled slowly, a quiet, controlled breath, like he was grounding himself before grounding you.
“It’s not stupid,” he said.
Your throat tightened unexpectedly. Something fragile inside you cracked just a little.
He saw it.
He always did.
And that was when Zayne moved quietly, deliberately shifting closer.
“Come here.”
At first, you weren’t sure you heard him right. Zayne wasn’t…huggy. Even when you were dating, he always waited for you to initiate touch.
But this time, he opened his arms.
You hesitated only a second before he gently took your shoulders and guided you into him.The moment your forehead touched his chest, everything hit at once, the leftover fear, the shaking, the exhaustion,
 and your hands curled into the front of his shirt in a small, desperate grip.
Zayne froze for one heartbeat.
Then he wrapped his arms around you.
One around your back.One cradling the back of your head.Pulling you fully, securely, into his warmth.
Not clinical.Not careful.Holding you like you were something precious.He lowered his chin so it rested atop your head. His heartbeat was slow and steady against your ear, a calm anchor pulling you back into yourself.
“I’ve got you,” he murmured.
Your fingers tightened in his shirt. “I’m sorry. I didn’t mean to wake you up—”
He cut you off with a quiet whisper against your hair:
“Stop apologizing.”
You swallowed hard. “I just… I hate feeling like this.”
His hand stroked slowly down your back, soothing, grounding, the kind of touch he rarely let himself give.“Of course you hate it,” he said softly. “But you don’t have to go through it alone.”
You exhaled shakily. “I didn’t want to bother you.”
“You can’t bother me.”
You pulled back slightly, trying to read his expression.
Zayne met your eyes with a softness he never showed in daylight, a look reserved exclusively for you.
“I’m not going anywhere,” he said, voice steadier than your breathing. “Not now. Not ever.”
And then as if the words weren’t enough, he pulled you back into his chest, holding you tighter, lowering his head so his lips brushed your temple.
You melted into him, the nightmare fading like mist in the sunrise.

Well, Vanessa had a talent for turning her "sickly-sweet" switch on the moment any grown-ups walked in; especially their parents. We're just having fun!"The grown-ups would sigh fondly, Vanessa would smile like an angel, and Jacob would swallow the sting in his throat.Maybe that's why Candle Cove always felt so important to him. When Jacob was alone with his thoughts.And on the screen, sailing across the foam-green ocean on the Laughingstock, next to Pirates Percy and Poppy, was Susan. Because while they craved the reality check Violence gave them, they needed the steady support that they weren’t all bad. They weren’t all gone yet.And when that ended, when Matthew Murdock ceased to exist, it was gone. Gone for both of them. Because suddenly Matt was in a basement without those soft words. It was all… violence. Simply violence.And when Foggy was back, it was fine. But Foggy was still normal. He hadn’t been ruined by Matt’s ash-covered hands yet.Foggy didn’t deserve what Matt put him through. He put up with it, sure, but it wasn’t what he deserved. He deserved a better friend. Matt had told him so, on drunken nights where something could’ve happened but didn’t. Foggy had always agreed with a soft, sad smile.“Maybe I do, but you’re who I have. And I don’t know about you, but I’m happy with who I got,” he said once.And when he died, that was all Matt could think about. He was happy to be friends with someone like Matt, and Matt had let him die.Matt had allowed his rivalries as the Devil slip to his friends, as he swore he never would.Maybe that’s why he retreated to Frank, after. That bullet helped him along, but he needed what they had solved so long ago. The way violence and affection could coexist. And maybe Matt didn’t crave that, exactly.Maybe at first, he craved to be beat down on. That he did kill his friend, and now he couldn’t even speak his name. Maybe he did need a wakeup call, and not a date with a therapist who didn’t know what was wrong.But that was a doorway back to old days. Back to simpler times. Back to times when he was still alive. Frank knew he was the substitute for Foggy, the only one Matt thought he deserved, but he was okay with that.Because at least he was helping. At least Matt was living for one more day, one more week, one more month.And then he wasn’t. But Frank wasn’t either. The explosion had killed them both. And maybe in those 7 minutes, Matt’s was filled with Foggy. Maybe Matt didn’t even think of Frank in those 7 minutes. But Frank thought of Matt, and that was the only thing that mattered.They had both wanted to be dead, in the end. Foggy was dead, and so part of Matt already was. And Frank, he had been a lifeline. But a lifeline means nothing if you don’t swim back to shore.Frank had lost Matt. He was still there, but simply a shell of who he was. All he was doing was coping, near the end. And it wasn’t enough to keep Frank going. And everyone responsible for his family’s death was dead by his hands, so did it really matter anymore?

Kenny stood in the hallway a little fearfully. He felt like his legs would collapse from underneath him at any moment and his head was spinning. He didn't understand how "Wow, Kenny, you stink!" turned into the sound of a bath running in the other room.Why couldn't Kyle just hose him off outside? He watched him walk down the hall to where he stood, now clad in his mom's rubber gloves that she used to wash dishes. "Are you ready?" he asked."What are you doing?" Kenny mumbled, not used to his voice without his parka on."My mom says I should wash your hair since it's all matted," he explained. "She's also gonna wash your clothes."Kenny felt out of place, but he also had to admit to himself that a bath and new clothes sounded nice. His skin was dry and itchy and his face felt oily. He didn't even want to think about his hair. "I can myself," he whispered quietly enough that Kyle didn't hear him. He didn't feel like talking anymore.Kyle led him back to the bathroom where the tub was full of big piles of bubbles. A cup and a rag sat on the edge of the bath, waiting to be used. Kenny just stood in the doorway for a few moments before Kyle gave him one more reassuring wave of his hand. "Come on," he said, "being clean is nice."Kenny fidgeted as he lowered himself into the bath, but it was warm. He liked the feeling. He still flinched when Kyle poured a cup of water on his head. He shivered as another downpour wet his hair. There was another and another as Kyle made sure to thoroughly drench his head. At least it didn't get in his eyes."You know your parents should be doing this stuff," Kyle told him as he uncapped the shampoo. "My mom makes me take care of my hair all the time."Kenny thought that was ironic with how much he wore his hat. Still, he doesn't say anything. He feels too vulnerable like this. Luckily, Kyle didn't seem to mind. He didn't rush when he lathered Kenny's head with a generous amount of shampoo. He was careful with it at first, like he was afraid to hurt him even though the two of them were wrestling a few minutes before. He got increasingly more rough as the tangled bits refused to undo themselves."I'm gonna get a comb," Kyle said, deserting Kenny for a moment as he rifled through a drawer. Kenny nodded, tucking his nose into his knees as he fluffed some bubbles in his hands.Then Kyle started to tug and pull at his hair with a comb. Tears began to poke their way out of Kenny's eyes, but he stayed strong. He kept going until he could run his hands through the strands and Kenny's head felt lighter."Okay now close your eyes," he informed, his voice gentle. Kenny obeyed, squeezing his eyes shut, knowing what came next.Another wall of water came barreling at his head until all the suds were gone again. Unfortunately, it wasn't over yet. Kyle was already lathering his head again before he could do anything.Once he was done Kyle told him, "Now we leave this in for a while. When you're dry it makes your hair really soft."Kenny nodded, going back to focusing on building little towers in the bubbles. It was like a city made of clouds, except Kenny knew clouds were just made of water and you couldn't really touch them. Still, it was fun to pretend.Kenny washed himself as Kyle took his dirty clothes to be cleaned and came back with a fresh pair of pajamas. He even made sure to keep his hair from getting wet. Kyle rinsed his hair out one last time and pulled the plug before handing him his towel."Okay, I'm gonna go help with dinner," he told Kenny with a smile. "You can come down whenever you're ready."Kenny didn't talk the rest of the night, he didn't need to. He enjoyed dinner with the Broflovskis and then fell asleep early on the couch.

Rows and rows of polished mahogany shelves seemingly stretched on till the end of the world. Upon them appeared to be as many books as there were stars in the sky, or blades of grass in the ground. The girl had never felt more out of place, covered from head to toe in dirt and wood shavings, face concealed by a dark mask and hood. 
Her journey here had been a prolonged and grueling one. Traveling from the Kingdom of the Others to the Central Empire was no simple feat, especially with all the laws in place guarding against border-crossing. Luckily, shady smugglers were more than willing to slip a person in with their cargo, for a plentiful sum, of course.
Weeks spent cramped in secret carriage compartments with wares from who knows where was exhausting. It seemed she might never rid the smell of illicit unicorn hides from her clothes, her hair, her very skin.

She could not get emotional right now. There was too much at stake.
Steeling herself with a deep breath, Sophia abandoned the books and crept deeper into the rows of shelves. Each step was carefully executed. Only occasionally would she depart from her path to check a nearby shelf and gauge her distance from the S’s.
The walking seemed to last for many hours, long into the night. However, she had no idea if this was reality, as the building didn’t contain a single window, probably to protect the books from damaging sun rays. Her only sources of light were oil lamps attached to the sides of each shelf. Their flames flickered wildly, ferocious animals trapped behind glass. Suddenly, the light from a lamp flung itself across a small novel on the shelf to her right. That’s when she saw it.
The lettering along the spine was thin and elegant, and stamped neatly at the bottom was “Simmons.” A great heat erupted within her. It was deadly and all-consuming, like a forest fire.
