Aziraphale had been looking forward to this day for months—but when he and Crowley stepped into their hotel room, he wanted to cry.Oh no.No no no.This was NOT tickety-boo.Not tickety-boo at all!Aziraphale had convinced Crowley to take him to Bath for a festival celebrating Jane Austen’s 250th birthday. Because so many people were in town for the festival, he and Crowley would have to share a room...a room that happened to have only one bed. While they shared the bed, the feelings they’d repressed for six millennia would come to light at last!Well, that was the plan anyway.But Aziraphale’s perfect plan had been ruined.The hotel roomhadTWObeds!Standing beside him, Crowley asked, “Which bed do you want?”Aziraphale told himself to put on a brave face as he answered. Instead he burst into tears.Confused, Crowley looked around the room to try to discover what had upset his best friend. It couldn’t be the beige walls that were almost the color of Aziraphale’s suit. The floral themed art on those walls was bland but inoffensive. The sole window offered a decent view of homes Aziraphale had called “charming.”  The room appeared to be clean and tidy—but maybe it was smaller than Aziraphale expected? “It’s not the greatest hotel room in the world, but we’ve stayed in much worse. Remember that time we had to sleep in a stable and a horse kicked me in the face?”Still crying, Aziraphale nodded. “Your poor face looked terrible, but you wouldn’t let me heal you. You didn’t want me to get in trouble.”“It worked out in the end. I told Hell I was injured fighting a big, scary angel.”“And they believed you?”“Beelzebub seemed suspicious, but a lot of low level demons were impressed. So...what made you so upset?”“The room...isn’t supposed to be like this. I told the young woman on the phone that I wanted...” Aziraphale trailed off as he tried to get his tears under control.“A minibar?” Crowley guessed. “If you’re feeling ‘peckish,’ we can order room service or go to a restaurant. I’ll make sure we get a table right away.”Aziraphale smiled through his tears. Although Crowley liked to pretend he wasn’t nice, the demon was always willing to take care of him. “I appreciate the offer, but I’m not hungry.”Crowley frowned. “You’re always hungry.”“Not always!”“Alright, fine. You’re not always hungry. But it’s unusual for you to turn down an offer of food. Whatever’s bothering you must be bad.” Crowley miracled himself into pajamas and lay down on the bed closest to the door. “If you’re not ready to tell me, I’m going to get some sleep. Good night, angel.”“Crowley, wait! Please don’t go to sleep just yet. I think...I think I am ready to tell you.”With a concerned expression on his handsome face, Crowley sat up in bed and stared at Aziraphale.“This room...it doesn’t have the right number of beds.”Crowley looked at Aziraphale as if he might be losing his mind.  “There are two beds and two of us.”“Indeed. But when I made my reservation…” Aziraphale lowered his eyes, unable to meet Crowley’s. “...I asked for a room with one bed.”“Oh.” Crowley’s eyes widened. “You wanted to share a bed...with me?”“Yes.”Crowley snapped his fingers. The twin beds disappeared and were replaced by a king size bed. “There you go. Get in, angel.”Smiling, Aziraphale changed into pajamas and climbed into the bed. “Thank you.”Crowley got into bed beside him. “Do you want to try to get some sleep...or did you have something else in mind?”“Well...” Aziraphale blushed. “My plan was that sharing a bed would lead to us revealing our true feelings for each other. I...I…oh dear. This is much harder than I thought it would be.”Crowley grinned. “You want to say that you care about me? Even though I’m a foul fiend and a servant of Satan and all that?”“I’ve never thought of you as a ‘foul fiend.’ Not really. You are and always have been my best friend and I…” As Aziraphale took the deepest breath of his existence, a line from Shakespeare’s Much Ado About Nothing popped into his mind. “I do love nothing in the world so well as you.”Crowley knew at once that Aziraphale was quoting one of his favorite plays. He held Aziraphale’s hands as he quoted another line from that play. “I love you with so much of my heart that none is left to protest.”Aziraphale giggled and embraced his demon. “Very nice.”“Angel...can I kiss you? Or is that going too fast?”“My dearest Crowley, I would be delighted to have you kiss me.”“Are you sure? Because once I start, I doubt I’ll be able to stop.”“I believe the same will be true for me. Go ahead, my dear.”Both were excited but nervous as their mouths met for the first time; Neither wanted to mess up a moment six millennia in the making. Yet their tentative kisses quickly became enthusiastic ones. Tentative touches became eager explorations of their best friend’s body.  Cuddling with Crowley, skin to skin, Aziraphale felt a happiness he’d never thought possible.His perfect plan had been perfect after all.

In the two weeks since Apo had finally returned home, Cherri had learned a few things about vampires that weren’t necessarily obvious unless you spent a lot of time around one. For example, that they were constantly cold.
Physical affection had always been present in their relationship, but after becoming a vampire, Apo would lean into Cherri and wrap their arms around her if she went longer than a minute or two without moving. While it could be a bit inconvenient at times, it was endearing enough that she mostly didn’t mind.
One such time, Cherri had been sitting on the couch in front of the fire, working on her sewing, when Apo leaned over and plopped their head in her lap.
“Careful there!” Cherri laughed, “I almost stabbed you with a pin!”
“Sorry.” Apo mumbled, already visibly relaxing as Cherri’s warmth seeped into her.
“It’s alright, just warn me next time.” Cherri put her sewing aside and ran her fingers through Apo’s hair, smiling as they visibly melted into the feeling. Soon, she began to notice a soft rumbling sound emanating from her partner’s chest.
“Are you purring?”
Apo looked suddenly embarrassed, shifting to try and hide her face. “Uh… maybe?”
“I didn’t know vampires purr! It’s cute.”
Apo just closed her eyes, her purring growing louder. It wasn’t exactly a response, but Cherri counted it as a success nonetheless.
She’d noticed Apo rarely seemed to close her eyes now, keeping them wide and watchful whenever the two of them ventured into the woods together (Apo refused to go into town at all anymore). It was only in these soft, quiet moments, when it was just the two of them at home, that Apo would let her eyes fall shut, trusting she was safe in her partner’s arms. It was a level of trust that Cherri didn’t take for granted.
Blossom had climbed up onto the couch and rested her head on Cherri’s knee with a whine for attention, clearly irritated that Apo was taking up all Cherri’s lap space. Cherri laughed and rubbed the dog behind the ears. “Aw, Blossom, don’t be jealous. You can share just this once.”
“No, you’re all mine.” Apo muttered sleepily, waving halfheartedly in Blossom’s general direction in a mockery of a claw swipe. “I’m cold, Blossom can wait her turn.”
“You’re always cold, love.”
“You’re always warm, problem solved.”
Cherri chuckled. “Well how am I supposed to argue with that sound logic?” She reached back to take the blanket off the couch and drape it over Apo as best she could. It wouldn’t do much since Apo couldn’t generate heat by herself, but it was more about the sentiment of the gesture anyway.
Cherri went back to her sewing for a couple more hours before she felt her eyelids start to droop. Apo’s breathing had already almost entirely vanished, something which had panicked Cherri the first couple of nights after Apo had returned, but that they had explained was a completely normal part of being a vampire. Since she didn’t technically need to breathe anymore, only doing it out of an unconscious instinct to blend in, Apo’s body didn’t bother continuing to take in oxygen while she was resting. She couldn’t properly sleep anymore either, instead entering a trancelike state of rest to regain energy.
“Hey Apo, we need to get up and go to bed.” Cherri gently shook Apo’s shoulder.
“No, I don’t wanna get up. Can’t we just sleep here?”
“Apo, I’m not a vampire. I’m gonna be so stiff in the morning if I fall asleep on the couch.” She gently pushed at Apo’s head to try and get her moving.
“Fine… Apo stumbled to her feet, scooping Cherri unceremoniously up into their arms like she weighed nothing at all. Cherri wasn’t sure she’d ever get over how unnaturally strong her partner was now.
Apo walked upstairs with Cherri in her arms and laid back down in bed before immediately slipping back into rest again, breathing fading away to just about nothing. Cherri leaned back against her chest and followed her into sleep.

Coiny was sitting outside with Firey. It was a cold day outside and Coiny was trying to sit as close to Firey as possible because he had on only a thin coat. Because of that, he had to hear him ramble on about his new baby, who had only hatched a day ago. After a while, he got very sick of that and decided to say something that came to his mind.“My children will beat your children up one day.” Coiny stated.
“Oh, will they now?” Firey retaliated.
“Uh-huh.”
“I bet they won’t!”
“Oh yes they will!”
“They won’t! Also I have to go, see ya!”
“Bye!”
And that’s all they had said to each other on that day.A few days later, Coiny was at Leafy’s house to help her with things. The baby, a little aspen leaf, was on Leafy’s chest in a baby carrier.
“Aww, just look at her!” Coiny said, distracting himself from sweeping once again to go over to the baby. He absolutely loved babies.
Leafy smiled and gently moved the baby away from him so he could get back on task.
“Well, soon you’re going to have a baby of your own,” Leafy said, “And then you can gush over it all you’d like.”
He paused. “I’m sorry, a what now?”
“A baby! Me and Firey are going to have a party for you and Pin and- Wait, no, I wasn’t supposed to tell you about that. Forget I said anything.”
“... Leafy, I’m not having a baby-”
“Shh! Just get back to sweeping now. I’m going to bed.”After Coiny was done with the cleaning, he went over to the park to walk and think things over. Why did they think he was going to be a father? Was it because of what he told Firey? No, he wasn’t that stupid. He thought for a while longer and then realized that this was actually a great thing. He and Pin get free cake and attention, which Pin loved. As he was walking, he saw Firey walking down the path too. He must’ve also needed a break, especially after spending so much time with a newborn.“Hey, Firey! How’s it going?”
“Good! Also, congratulations on the baby!”
“Thanks. Me and Pin are so excited to see her.” Coiny knew this was a lie of course, but he needed to keep it up if he still wanted cake.
“And I’m so excited to see Aspen crush her when they both get older.”
“You mean when my daughter crushes yours.”
“As if! Also, can you two stop by me and Leafy’s place this afternoon? We want you to see our new couch.”
Coiny already knew what was happening. “Yeah, sure.”Once he got home, he immediately rushed upstairs to tell Pin about the party. Normally he would also try to keep it a secret from her, but he wanted to make sure she didn’t accidentally let it slip that they weren’t expecting a baby. When he got upstairs and to their bedroom, he saw Pin on the bed, wrapping an egg that was about half his size, which wasn’t much anyways considering he was so short, in a blanket. Coiny stared at it for a while.“Pin, is that- Is that a-”
“Oh, I forgot to tell you. Whoopsies.”
She handed him the egg. It was scarlet and the most beautiful thing he had ever seen. She was looking at it like it was the second most beautiful thing she had ever seen, the first being paprika.
“Oh, by the way, Leafy and Firey want us at their place in a few minutes.” He said, holding the egg as carefully as he could. “They want us to see their new couch.”They went over to their house and knocked on the door. As soon as she opened the door, Leafy shoved them onto the couch, gently since they had the egg with them, and gave them a slice of cake each. Firey wasn’t there at the moment because he was upstairs with Aspen. After a few hours, they all noticed there was a big crack in the side of the egg. Leafy then ushered them out of the house so they could go home and watch the baby be hatched there.Once they got home, they sat down on the bed, the egg between them, and watched. At one point they stopped watching and watched TV because it was taking a long time, but then they went right back to waiting for the egg to hatch. After about an hour, it finally happened. Out of the egg came a red disc, like a token. Coiny scooped her up and placed her on Pin because babies need contact when they’re first born.“Awww, she’s so cute,” Pin said, staring at the token. “Like paprika.”
Coiny took a seat next to her. “She has your eyes.”
“And your… everything. Wow.”
Then they both fell asleep, holding their daughter between them.

Azriel Berdara was known for many things. Being late was not one of them.
And yet here he was, trapped in his own bed, late to meet his brother at the River House.
But, he couldn't bring himself to regret it one bit. Looking down, he pressed another kiss to Gwyn's temple, enjoying the way she sighed in contentment, and curled in closer to his body. They'd had a late night, as always, enjoying their midnight spar, before enjoying other late-night activities. Now, Gwyn's face was buried in the crook of his shoulder, her breath tickling his neck, and the familiar weight of her body sprawled over his wing, pinning it under her, and rendering him wholly immobile.
He was seriously beginning to consider waking his mate up. He really needed to go over his findings in Autumn with Rhysand, but feared the consequences if he deprived Gwyn from her "hard-earned beauty rest," as she put it.
Fuck it, he thought. I'll make it up to her later. He flexed his back, trying to pull his wing free. Nothing. Frowning, he pulled harder. This time, he got an inch of movement. In response, Gwyn's arm lazily arced around, narrowly avoiding his face, before wrapping around his shoulder. Just before he could try a third time, he felt the familiar sensation of his brother's claws on his mental shields.
Where are you?
Stilling, he responded, I'm stuck.
He could almost hear Rhysand's amused grin across the bridge linking their minds. After a moment, his brother asked, the fearsome spymaster of the Night Court, is stuck, how exactly?
Well, he thought, mildly annoyed, my mate has decided that my wing is far superior as a mattress, compared to our actual mattress.
There was a second of silence, before Rhysand started laughing. Grumbling quietly under his breath, careful not to wake Gwyn, he asked, I'm never going to hear the end of this, am I?
No, his brother responded.
No, you are not. After a moment, he added,
We can talk later. Enjoy your morning with Gwynnie.
You better not tell Cassian about this, he said, not waiting for Rhysand's inevitable disagreement, before closing his mind again.
Turning his head, he buried his face in his mate's hair, inhaling her sweet scent.
Home, he thought, before he wrapped his other wing around them, joining Gwyneth in the warm embrace of sleep.

Bokuto was the last member from his roster to retire from the MSBY Black Jackals, and reluctantly so. Atsumu, Hinata, and Sakusa had already retired years prior, and the rest, long before that. Bokuto wanted to play until he was at least forty-five, but after his last injury cost them the game, he realized that there was nothing he could do besides retire.
It sucked, not being able to go to practice anymore, and when he did, he was usually shoo’d off by the coach for moping around the gym with a depressing aura and a limp, eyebrows twitching occasionally when names that weren't his own were called to make kills.
It was another night where Bokuto was forbidden from coming to practice. It was ‘for his own good’—at least that’s what the managers had said—as his urge to play would only grow, and not being able to would depress him more.
Bokuto didn’t go home that night, instead, he took a detour towards the park near his apartment. He pulled the strings of the hoodie tightly and the hood scrunched up, closing around his nose. He wanted to scream in frustration, but he’d look like a mad man and for the first time in his life, he didn’t want any attention on him.
Grunting, he looked down at his feet as he tugged open the hood a bit. He could feel the oncoming burning sensation through his ankle the longer he kept his weight on it, and for some sick reason he wanted to stay like that, almost punishing himself for even getting an injury in the first place. He was careless, and he knew it would take him longer to heal, so maybe he deserved the pain.
No, he didn’t.
He yelped the second it felt like too much, and scrambled over to one of the nearby benches to lift the weight off his foot. Tears pricked the corner of his eyes and he leaned his head back, breathing out slowly. His hands balled into fists and he punched the empty space beside him.
“Dammit!”
“Whoa, what did the poor bench ever do to you?”
Bokuto opened his eyes slowly when he heard the voice. He looked over and he saw a very familiar, mischievous grin.
“Kuroo?” Bokuto’s eyes widened as he looked at him. It had been a while since he’d seen the guy. Then again, he’d been so busy with volleyball.
He eyed him head to toe. Kuroo was wearing a hoodie similar to his own, shorts, and more importantly, there was a kid latched onto his leg. Bokuto had to rub his eyes and blink harshly to make sure he was seeing right.
“Is that your-”
“Yup,” Kuroo said simply. The hair on the kid’s head almost matched Kuroo’s, it was just… softer. It looked like it could have been styled if it wanted to be.
“Kou, you remember Bokuto Koutarou, you know, number twelve from the Black Jackals?” Kuroo stated proudly, as he moved to sit next to Bokuto, pulling the boy onto his lap.
Bokuto’s heart clenched at that.
“Was,” he murmured, shoulders noticeably slouching.
Kuroo turned to him, surprised, “What?”
“I was number twelve, I’m… officially retired, as of a few days ago,” he explained, dropping his head into his hands.
“Wow,” was all Kuroo said, pulling Kou—who had been silently taking in the conversation—closer to him, “I guess the news didn’t break yet, huh? At least, I didn’t get any information…” he trailed off, saying the last part quieter.
Bokuto shook his head slightly, “They wanted to make sure I could talk about it without… bursting into tears,” His bottom lip trembled at the thought, and he bit his lip to suppress his wavering voice.Kuroo stayed silent and pressed his lips together. After a few seconds, he placed a hand on Bokuto’s shoulder, gripping his sleeve.
“You played a good game, Bo.”
Bokuto couldn’t keep silent any more. A soft sniffle shifted to quiet sobs into his hands as he pressed his palms against his eyes. His tears felt hot against his skin and he finally cried, releasing all the pent up emotions he’d been carrying for the entire week.
Kuroo stayed silent next to him and let him cry it out. For as long as he had known Bokuto, volleyball, attention, and being a star was everything to him. So, as much as his mouth was itching to crack a joke to cheer him up, he knew Bokuto needed this moment of vulnerability.
“He’s crying,” The seven year old whispered to Kuroo, who cupped his hand over his mouth.
Bokuto heard him however and it snapped him back into reality. He rubbed his face harshly and with another sniffle, he cleared his throat.“Sorry.”
Kuroo shook his head, “Don’t worry about it. If you didn’t say anything, I’d’ve probably asked how you were, and the same thing would’ve happened.”
Bokuto cracked a smile and rubbed off the tear stains from his cheek with his sleeve. His eyes moved to Kou again.“Hey, hey, hey, Kou, I’m Koutarou,” He gasped weakly, his eyes going to Kuroo, “Heeey, our names are similar! Did you name him after me, bro?”
Kuroo scoffed and rolled his eyes, “How’d I know you’d say that. No I didn’t, don’t flatter yourself.”
Bokuto scrunched his nose and waved a finger at the boy, “Well I’m still taking that win. Kou Kuroo.”

Thanks to the Vicodin, House can't drink anymore, but he still likes to pretend. Sometimes he'll pour a finger of flat gingerale or some other non-alcoholic drink into a glass, open a bottle of scotch (the same bottle every time), and sip the gingerale while he smells the scotch. Smell contributes so much to the taste of things that sometimes, if he's not really thinking about it, he can actually taste the liquor.Of course, he can only do that at home. When he goes to a bar he orders a coke and lets people think it's a rum and coke, or orders water and lets them think it's vodka, or...there's a variety of dodges he can use, and House knows them all. He uses them all, too, because he does still go to bars. Partly because while Wilson never actually gets drunk (just like he never actually sleeps with all the women he flirts with), he's still infinitely more relaxed with a beer or two in him.But mostly, House goes to bars because that's the only place he knows where you can still play darts.Okay, so there are probably darts clubs and darts leagues and who knows what else, but House isn't about to join some back slapping social exercise with plastic yellow and blue team jackets just because the infarction had left him his hand to eye coordination, even if it had taken his leg. Besides, in bars he sometimes wins money playing darts."You're not even paying attention to the points anymore, are you?" Wilson asked, a half empty bottle dangling between his fingers. It was only his second, but House suspected he'd nurse it for the rest of the night."Of course I'm paying attention to the points," House said, and let fly with his last dart. It thunked solidly into the outermost ring, forming a perfectly horizontal line with the other two darts. The middle one was only through the bullseye because that was where the line went. Really. "How else would I know where to aim?""Just concentrate on the little red dot," Wilson said dryly.House limped up to the board to retrieve his darts and shot Wilson a disappointed look on his way back. "The same target every time? But that would be boring."Wilson took a drink from his bottle and shook his head as House positioned himself for another round. Strangely enough, everyone else had stopped playing after he'd started making patterns with his turns. "If you wanted to spice up the game, we could always blindfold you," Wilson suggested. House had to turn away from the board to look at him, because his friend sounded more than half serious.James was smiling, so House quirked an eyebrow at him. "You have a blindfold on hand? What have you been doing on your breaks, Dr. Wilson?""We'd have to improvise," Wilson smirked a little and waved his tie a little."The voice of experience, I suspect," House said, smiling. He turned back to board and let fly with his first dart. "I was thinking something more along the lines of shooting an apple off of someone's head." His second dart found its target."The idea you trying to shoot an apple off of someone's head is frightening."House planted his third dart and turned to appropriate Wilson's set. "What," he said as he gathered them up, "you don't think I'm the archery type? I think I could be very good." Two more projectiles sailed through the air and embedded themselves in the battered board."It's not that. I just don't think you're the type to aim for the apple."The last dart completed the pattern. House turned to Wilson and found him shaking his head over the smiley face the darts marked out. "Well, that depends, doesn't it?" House said philosophically.Wilson raised his eyebrows. "On what?"House grinned at him. "On whose head is holding up the apple."--End--

Hansol doesn’t say anything either, does it as if it’s second nature, as if it’s his obligation.
They don’t talk about a lot of things these days.
Seungkwan still thinks of Hansol as his best friend, it’s been over thirteen years, and he thinks they’ll never be able to rid themselves of that title. They aren’t as close as they used to be, however, a fact that sits uncomfortably in the back of his mind.
If Hansol has something he wants to go do, there is a long list of people he’ll invite before even thinking of Seungkwan, who, in a similar fashion, finds it harder to tell Hansol things he used to share with ease. He confides in Seokmin or Jeonghan more often nowadays. He pretends his heart doesn’t feel like it’s ripping in two anytime he’s with one of them and sees a photo in their group chat of Hansol with someone else.
Seungkwan looks at the orange in Hansol’s hand, watches the way he skillfully pushes the peel back without even looking at it. He wonders if it’s always been this way, or if Hansol learned how to peel oranges for him. Seungkwan always makes a mess, digs his fingers in too deep, presses too hard on the flesh and deals with the consequences in a stickiness that doesn’t quite go away, even when clean. He thinks he loves the same way he peels oranges. He wonders if Hansol does too.

Hansol and Seungkwan sat together, pressed their shoulders into each other until they couldn’t possibly get any closer. They used to do that a lot, try to mesh their bodies into one, would hope that one day it actually worked so they’d never have to part — it never did.
Seungkwan pulled the orange from his bag, and before he could even think about it, he pressed the citrus into Hansol’s waiting palm. It hit him then, that this was a thing, another part of their routine. Hansol still needed to look at the oranges then.
“Doesn’t the smell bother you?” Seungkwan had asked, because he couldn’t bring himself to ask the question he really wanted to. Couldn’t bring himself to ask Hansol why he would peel oranges for him — if Hansol loved Seungkwan the way he loved the other.
“It smells like you,” Hansol had responded. They didn’t talk about it. They never talked about it. Seungkwan just laughed and rolled his eyes, pressed his head into Hansol’s shoulder, wished they could become one just for a minute. Maybe they did.
Hansol finishes peeling the orange, pops a stolen carpel into his mouth before handing the rest of it to Seungkwan. He wonders if the scent is still his. He wonders if Hansol holds his hands close to his face to remember a time they used to be closer. He wonders, more bitterly, if Hansol feels anything when he washes the scent away.
What happened to us, he wants to ask, instead he accepts the fruit. He bites at a segment, feels the way it separates under his teeth, wonders if Hansol would do this for him for the rest of their lives. Would they still be holding onto the title of best friends while pulling away from each other in another decade? His stomach churns uncomfortably and he bites down too hard. He fights to ignore the pain that settles in his mouth and the blood pooling from his tongue. Pretends the metallic and citrus mix well together.

“You’re soaked…” Strohl exclaimed with all the poise of a concerned mother. Taking another clothespin on the line, he finished hanging up a dress shirt, along with a cloth that seemed to serve no real purpose. “I’m about done with laundry, so you can use the machine, if you’d like.”
 Will could’ve smirked if the energy wasn’t spent on shivering. Far as he observed, Strohl didn’t exactly utilize the gauntlet runner’s more advanced facilities, vying instead to take on old habits from home unless absolutely necessary, including using the basin as a means to do washing by hand.
 Instead, his gaze drifted towards the floor, bringing his arms together at his torso and sinking deeper into his sagging coat.
 “Actually, this is all I have.”
 Saying it out loud made his face burn. There was nothing really wrong with it, he guessed. At least nothing to be ashamed of. Maybe. Yet the simple act of admitting he’d been wearing the same clothes every day was… something. Didn’t acknowledge it much until seeing others rotate through casual and formal garb.
 With a wry chuckle, and ‘neat freak’ oozing from him as he focused on straightening his clothing, the clemar replied with, “You’re joking,” in the most amused yet unamused tone possible.
 Will silently debated leaving. Strohl finally looked back.
 “…Oh. Have you really…?”
 Slow nod. Painfully slow nod.
 Strohl’s brow furrowed. Taking a step back from his work, he gave his captain a once-over.
 Surely, the elda thought, he didn’t look that dirty or smelled. Bathing wasn’t exactly his favorite activity, but he did do it often. Only thing he ever took the time to wash was his coat, and his actual clothes displayed minimal wear and tear.
 “I’m aware our funds are to go towards the campaign, but if you’d told us, we would’ve found a tailor.” With a short breath, the clemar mostly closed the gap between them. “Don’t want you catching a cold or some other illness.”

Strohl recreated distance just for the coat, frowning as it continued to drip with rain. Wasn’t like the wearer wasn’t any less wet, fabric clinging to him. It was hastily draped on the curve of the basin, Strohl gesturing Will to follow him to their sleeping quarters.
 Less than a minute later, Will was gifted oversized garments.

It felt like Billy was really expressing how he felt about Stu for the first time in a long time.As he sat on his bed, Stu knew that, logically, Billy was just upset again, saying things he didn’t mean out of anger. Still, it felt like something more, something deeper now.The longer Stu thought about it, the more he worried. Was he too much? He’d never really thought about the way he acted around people until now.Stu bit his lip, pulling his knees to his chest. Tears pricked at the corners of his eyes as fear started to mix with the sadness. Maybe everyone found him annoying. Maybe Billy had just said what everyone else was thinking. Maybe everyone would leave him because he couldn’t control himself. Maybe-Tears ran down his cheeks, and he buried his face in his knees. His parents weren’t home, out to dinner again, so Stu sobbed. He sobbed uncontrollably, his whole body shaking as he mumbled broken phrases like “I’m sorry” and “I’ll just stop.”He stayed like that for a long time. Eventually, his breathing was returning to normal, even as the tears kept flowing. He pulled his phone out of his pocket and looked at it for a moment before he dialed Billy’s number, praying he’d pick up.Billy’s voice came through the phone, uttering a scratchy “Hello?” Stu let out a shaky breath.“Billy, man, I’m sorry…” He tried to keep his voice steady, but his heart started to race again, and he felt more tears coming.“What’s wrong, Stu?” Billy asked through the phone, sounding confused and maybe even a little worried.“I’m sorry, Billy… I’ll do better, I promise…” Stu’s voice broke on the last word, and he let out a sob. Billy hung up.When he heard the click of the phone going dead, he started sobbing again. This time, though, his crying fit was interrupted by a knock on his window.He turned to look and saw a figure through the curtains. He didn’t even think about it before he got up and let Billy in.As soon as Billy got through the window, Stu hugged him and started mumbling “I’m sorry” over and over again until it seemed like those were the only words he knew.“Stu, it’s okay, shh…” Billy rubbed Stu’s back as Stu cried. Billy moved the two of them to Stu’s bed, sitting them down.“N-no, man, it’s not okay…” Stu wailed. “Am I… annoying, Billy?”Billy’s breath caught in his throat at Stu’s words. All of a sudden, he realized what had Stu so worked up.“Am I really too m-much?” Billy took Stu’s face in his hands and pulled him back to look into his aqua eyes.“Stu. You aren’t too much. Maybe you’re a lot, but you’re never too much. I’m sorry I got mad at you earlier.” Billy reassured the boy, kissing him softly. Stu melted and fell against Billy’s chest, pushing him to lay down. Stu cuddled up to Billy as he cried, softer now.Eventually, Stu’s crying quieted and his breathing evened out.“I’m sorry, Billy..” Stu mumbled, though his voice was steadier now.“You didn’t do anything wrong, Stu.” Billy ran a hand through Stu’s short dirty blonde hair.“I love you, no matter what.” Stu’s breath caught. This was one of the only times Billy had said those words.“I love you too, Billy, so much…” Stu said, tears of happiness pricking at his eyes. Billy wiped them away.“No more crying. It’s okay.” Billy cooed. He held Stu as he slowly fell asleep. When Stu was asleep at last, breathing finally steady, Billy stared at the ceiling. He looked down at Stu’s sleeping figure and smiled, then closed his eyes and joined Stu in sleep.

In fact, only two people seemed to know what had happened: Charlie, who returned to the hotel with loose hair and blood on her shoes, and Angel Dust himself, who staggered behind her, a hand clasped in her claws, mascara running down his cheeks in clumps.
“Damn, that’s an ugly bruise.” Husk clucked, polishing a glass. His ears flicked in surprise as Angel unexpectedly broke away from Charlie and started straight for the elevator. He didn’t look back, not even as she called after him:
“Angel, wait! Wait, let me help!”
He froze. It wasn’t until she was quite literally forcing the doors open for him to turn around and plead, in a voice ragged, “You’ve already done enough, Charlie. Now let me go.”
She stepped back and he gazed past her, at the loosely gathered denizens of the hotel. His eyes unfocused as the doors shut and the old mechanism clanked to life.
Charlie stepped back and almost tripped into Alastor.
Clap. Clap. Clap.
The Radio Demon was smiling at her with such amusement it almost looped around to pride. “Excellent work, Charlie. Way to take initiative!”
“Well- I- I couldn’t just let him hurt him!” She turned around, saying it as though those words were all she could hold onto. She emphatically gestured at nothing in particular, before curling hands into fists and sucking in a breath, “What kind of a FRIEND would I be if- if- if- oh…oh my god.”
The reality of the blood on her clothes seemed to come through, as Vaggie quickly looped an arm around her waist to steady her.
“Easy babe. Just,” she guided Charlie towards one of the couches, forcing her stiff girlfriend to sit. A gray hand squeezed hers, “...Tell us what happened.”
“I would so very much like to hear it from you, though I’m sure word will spread throughout hell in a matter of…oh…hours.” Alastor materialized on his favorite armchair. Nifty scurried onto his lap while Husk stalked over from behind the bar, eyes still set to the elevator. Pentious also emerged, wringing his hands as his egg boys poked each other.
Charlie sucked in a breath. She had to tell them – her closest friends in the world deserved to know.
Something in her said, maybe I should wait until Angel can be here to discuss it...
A much more grounded voice reasoned, well, you don’t know when that’s going to be.
Oh, god, you’re right! I don’t!
Is he okay? I should check on him. But he said –
 shit! What do I… how do I …
“In. Out.” Vaggie squeezed her hand. “Remember to breathe, babe.”
She did, until the world slowed its spinning.
“I followed Angel Dust to his work,” Charlie finally began, quickly, brittly. “And I understand that was definitely a violation of boundaries on my part, but I just…really wanted to get him some time off. He’s been working so much and it’s just not fair, and he always comes home exhausted… Maybe I could do something…since I’m the Princess of Hell and all…”“...you ought to command more authority, mm?” Alastor filled in.
Vaggie shifted, uncomfortably. Husk noticed this and his tail lashed.
“Yes. Because what kind of ruler am I if I can’t protect the people I care about?” Charlie made a fist with her other hand, fangs bared, “and it would have been one thing if Angel just had a strict mean boss…but he- Valentino - he was worse than anything I could’ve imagined.”
“I’m not surprised,” Husk grumbled and Alastor made a small noise of amusement.
Sir Pentious flicked golden eyes from Charlie to Alastor, “V-Valentino, isssssssn’t he one of the Veesssssssssssss…?”
Vaggie shot them a glare. Let her finish.
“So I did what any good friend would in that situation.” Charlie finally got out. “I don’t want to give the specifics on what he was doing to Angel because that is sensitive information, but-”
“It involves the black eye.” Alastor stated, informatively.
“And the late night drinking sessions,” Husk added.
“Oh! And Angel’sssssssss limp!”
“So a physically abusive porn director. I’m sure we can infer the rest without getting into it,” Vaggie paraphrased, looking back to her girlfriend. Charlie, like a guilty puppy, would not meet her eye.
“What happened to him? Is that why you’re covered in blood? Can I taaaaaste it?” Nifty bounced on Alastor’s knee, her one pupil dilated to the size of a dinnerplate.
“He won’t be a problem anymore.” Charlie said, looking at the floor.
“So you hurt him?”
“Ohh, did you make him bleed?”
A beat passed.
“Is…he ssssstill with us?”
“Sinners can’t die, unless by…”Angelic will, be it steel or holy light.
Charlie was half angel - they all knew this, even if she never brought it up. Now, positively glowing with holy determination, she put her hands to her heart and said, fiercely, “I protected my friend, the way I’d protect any one of you. Because redemption is possible, as long as you are safe and supported.”
Husk flicked a look at Alastor, whose smile only widened.
Pentious started to clap. When he realized no one else was joining in, he quickly stopped.

Life in the countryside can be quite peaceful, especially in a small town. With such a small and tight-knit community it’s normal for everyone to know everyone else, and for the young priest of the only church in town, nothing is better than the kindness and support among neighbours. As the congregation gathers inside the old stone walls Lyney greets them all with a smile, the good book held tightly in his arms, a humble modest rosary hanging from his neck over his robes. Everything he could ever want, everything he could ever need, it’s all there right inside the stone walls of that old church, and he can’t thank the holy father enough for the blessings he has bestowed upon him. Lyney watches as everyone takes a seat, Lady Furina is always at the front right next to Monsieur Neuvillette, Miss Navia and Miss Clorinde always seat near the back, and Miss Charlotte seats politely at the middle row ready to share her latest publication as soon as the sermon ends. By the time he closes the door, Miss Chevreuse and the foreign seamstress Chiori are already sitting, their extravagant hats make them stand out but Lyney thinks them charming, and he can see his dear brother Freminet taking his own seat towards the back. Et ne nos inducas in tentationem, sed libera nos a malo, Amen”“Amen” The crows utters in response, and he knows that god has heard them.Today’s sermon is not anything grand, and he doesn’t deem it too important, but the words of The Lord are sacred and he treats them all with the same level of respect.“... As he takes a step towards the last row of seats the door closes behind him, his gaze never leaves the young priest. “I warn you, as I warned you before, that those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God…”The rest of the sermon passes in the blink of an eye, singing praises of the Lord’s infinite love and benevolence, but there’s something that bothers Lyney greatly, even if he doesn’t let it show. The outsider keeps looking at him the whole time, and the way he smiles makes the priest’s heart beat fast, full of uneasiness. He shouldn’t judge, but there’s something about him that makes him wary. Lyney tries his best to ignore the feeling as he prepares to give his congregation the eucharist, and for a moment he manages to lose himself into his work once again, until he’s face to face again with that man. He watches as the stranger slowly but surely drops to his knees, even while on the ground he still looks big. His strong hands reach for his robe, placing a kiss on the fabric before raising his head to look at him. Lyney can’t put a name to the feeling that invades him so thoroughly, but he still places the eucharist on the man’s open mouth, and with a dignified expression he quells the urge to run.“Father Lyney, right?” The man finally addresses him directly, his voice so deep that it sends shivers down Lyney’s spine.“That would be me, I guess you are new here, Mister…?”“Wriothesley, my name is Wriothesley” The man, who now has a name, extends his hand to him in a gesture of good will. Pain, a pain that shakes the earth at your feet, you’re acutely aware of the pounding in your chest. Pain. A flash of red and it was over.Death had taken Vincent. Families of all shapes and sizes would huddle on their sofas, popcorn in hand, just to see Vincent shout out his killer catch phrase “Baby you’re the greatest on TV”!Fans of the TV show host would come far and wide just to get a glance from the shining star. He strutted onto the stage, his steps meaningful and echoing in the stadium. Thousands of onlooking eyes beamed at Vincent, seeking wisdom. More intense than any lust he had ever known, Power.After that event Vincent handed out flyers in his town, advertising his new movement. With him at the head he would make all their problems disappear, as long as they trusted him. Not as many came to this movement as the official celebrity event, but it was a sizable turnout. The theater smells like dust and forgotten velvet. The kind of smell that clings to curtains that have absorbed too many monologues, too many breaths, too many ghosts pretending to be someone else. I sit near the back because I don’t like being seen when I’m not sure who I am supposed to be. The lights haven’t dimmed yet. They leak a weak amber across the rows, catching in the floating dust like dead stars.
I came because of a poster. It was taped crookedly on a lamppost near the café I used to haunt. The title was what caught me first—Mirrors. Weird choice for a play, I thought. The name beneath it: Adeline Alvarez. I had read that name before, in some feature about a rising actress who specialized in method acting, the kind that makes people uneasy because she doesn’t stop performing even after the curtain falls. I wasn’t planning to come here. But something in me shifted when I saw the date—tonight—and I didn’t even remember deciding until I was already inside, buying a ticket from a woman who didn’t look me in the eye.
Now the program sits folded on my lap, damp from my palms. The synopsis says nothing useful. “A meditation on identity, memory, and performance.” The kind of phrase meant to protect you from what it really is. My seat creaks when I shift. I feel like I’ve intruded on something private, but that’s nothing new.
The lights dim. A collective hush rises, the kind that belongs to church and confessionals. The stage is bare except for a single chair and a hanging bulb. Then she walks in.
Adeline.
At least, that’s who she’s supposed to be. But I know the way she walks. The careful hesitation in her right step, the faint inward turn of her ankle like she’s trying to fold herself smaller. That used to be mine.
When she sits on the chair, the breath leaves my chest as if she’s taken it. The silence stretches, and I start to think maybe I should leave. But then she lifts her head and speaks—and the voice is mine too.
Not just the tone. The rhythm. The tremor. The small, defensive lilt I didn’t know was audible until it was.
“I was never good at being seen,” she says. “Not because I feared it, but because I didn’t believe it could happen.”
The line comes from somewhere far back in my memory—a page in a notebook, the kind I filled in late nights when I was trying to understand why my reflection never looked like me. My stomach tightens. My hand goes cold.
The play isn’t inspired by me. It is me.
For a moment I think it’s paranoia. But then she says the next line, and I remember exactly where it’s from: the first entry in a diary I wrote when I was twenty-one, one I burned three years ago in a trash bin behind my apartment.
“I used to imagine an audience in my room,” Adeline continues, looking out into the dark. “Someone to watch me live so I didn’t have to.”
I press my fingers to my lips. The audience doesn’t know. They think it’s fiction. But I feel my own words vibrating through another throat, shaped by another mouth, and something in me begins to fracture.
The performance unfolds slowly, deliberately, as if time itself has been instructed to obey her pacing. Scenes dissolve into one another without blackouts—she just shifts posture, tone, light, and suddenly we’re somewhere else. My old apartment. My childhood kitchen. The bus seat where I wrote lists of people I would never be. She recites them all. Every line, every pause, every shameful thing I wrote to myself when no one was watching.
I don’t understand how she got it. I don’t understand why she wants it. But instead of horror, what rises is something stranger, warmer. She’s perfect. She moves the way I never managed to. Her small hesitations look deliberate, meaningful. When she bites her lip, the audience leans in. When I used to do that, people told me it looked nervous.
They’re applauding me, I think. Or the version of me that deserved applause.
I don’t leave.
Act One—if there is such a thing—bleeds into something quieter. A light isolates her face. Her eyes are glassy, reflecting the bulb overhead like she’s drowning under water.
“I didn’t want to be loved,” she whispers. “I wanted to be recognized. To be told I existed correctly.”
The words land like a knife I once hid under the floorboard of memory. They shouldn’t hurt anymore, but they do, because she delivers them without apology. As if they’re not pathetic. As if they’re holy.
I start to feel watched. Not by her, but by the audience. They don’t look at me, but somehow they see me through her. My skin crawls. I want to shrink, but I can’t stop looking at her.
Every tilt of her head is a resurrection. She resurrects a version of me I killed quietly—the girl who wanted to be an artist, the one who thought the world might make sense if she could only name it. I used to think I failed because I wasn’t brave enough. Watching her, I wonder if I failed because I wasn’t beautiful enough to be forgiven.

A regressor.
I imagine you’re familiar with the concept?
Someone going back in time to change something or… more often than not, reliving the same stretch of time over and over, nigh on endlessly, in search of some impossible to reach goal.
It goes by many names; ‘the perfect timeline’ ‘the best possible ending’ ‘the epilogue’ even the classic ‘Happily Ever After.’
Depending on who you ask, more than the name what that goal entails is different.
Could be the timeline where everyone survives or the timeline where just that one specific person makes it to the end… or something entirely different.
You chose to call that goal normalcy.
You wanted a world where the people you loved could live in everyday peace.
And you achieved it.
After so many attempts, so many failures… enough that trying to put a number to them would only make your head hurt.
You were able to create that world for them.
You have rewritten the world to be a peaceful and mostly mundane place for everyone you cared about. They now face mundane crises as they live normal lives… instead of the nightmarish fight for survival they had to face alongside you.
Knowing that all of them can enjoy this gentler world is everything you have ever wanted.
Though you will likely never get to meet them again.
The cost of this peaceful world you brought forth was one you didn’t take lightly. In exchange for the power to rewrite the world…
You have been completely erased.
At least… you should have been erased.
Every trace of your existence has vanished. Not a single soul remembers your name, your face, or even your voice. You’ve vanished from any photo you were featured in, any belongings you had in a childhood home no longer exist. The person who was you does not exist in this world. Your family has forgotten you, your companions have forgotten you…
The man you loved has forgotten you.
All that remains is… you.
Stubbornly still here, wandering as a shadow through a world that no longer holds a place for it… you.
You won’t be like this much longer… you believe you only have a few more years at best before the debt of this world’s recreation is finally paid in full.
You’re already feeling the toll being taken on your body… you’re invisibly deteriorating more and more everyday.
What will happen when your time is up, you often wonder…
Will you simply collapse one day, your first and only tangible mark on this world your unidentifiable corpse?
Will you return to the abyss you cast yourself into and fall into an endless dream?
Or will you simply vanish? Your body scattered on the wind like dandelion seeds that will never meet the ground.
No matter what your ending will be… you have long accepted that it will arrive soon, and you will finally fade away for good when it does.
No room for regret, you made this decision.
You would never choose differently, even if given infinite chances to do so… you would always make the same choice.
You decided that it was for the best that you vanish in obscurity… you’d made peace with the fact you’d never see them all again…
Until fate drew you to Stardew Valley…
The place your former companions now call home.
A cousin you’d only met in passing as a kid received a letter from your grandfather who had recently passed… and he dumped it onto the first unlucky looking stranger he saw, calling it a gift…
That stranger happened to be you.
You didn’t have the chance to return it and refuse the offer. By the time you recognized him he had already left… grumbling about how stupid the request was. How ‘Grandpa should have known he’d never take it.’

So the Kyr'tsad wasn't some secret organization on Mandalore, well not mostly anyways, it was separate. Daisy had a fairly good idea of who had formed it, and she hated it. She had a few hours before reaching Krownest. Hopefully Wren would listen to her at the least.

Sirens blared in tune with the beating of Riley's heart, a deafening melody line breaking the expected silence tonight. Riley's vision was blurry, as their hands felt the somewhat rough material of the stretcher they were laying on. A few people in uniform surrounded them, saying things that they couldn't decipher.
Their chest was heaving and the feeling of dread and panic made their stomach heavy, but they couldn't remember why. Pain seared through every atom of their being, as a screeching noise tore through the air.
Shut up already,
thought Riley as their throat ached. Throat ached? They realize the noise was coming from their own mouth. What was happening? Why were there people everywhere? What are the sirens for?Riley groaned as they felt their body being wrapped up tight by something soft and rough at the same time. Their arms and face and legs were bound, but they couldn't tell with what. They briefly made out the words
"You'll be okay"
within the cacophony of noises. The screams echoing in the background mixed in with every noise let loose in the dark of the night, swelling and stirring together like some kind of choir. And then it was all too much. They felt their hands on their throat, their heart in their stomach. Every single atom and skin covering their body felt like they were on fire.
Their breaths came out in ragged puffs and coughs, battered and abused by their screaming and screeching. Riley felt heat in their eyes as they welled up with tears. They cry out, coming out as a monstrous noise. The people surrounding them put them up on a machine, and put a mask on their mouth to ease their breathing, maybe. Genuinely, what was happening? It was all going so fast. Who were these people?
Riley's head filled with confusion and fear. Were they being kidnapped or something? I
want my mommy and daddy. It was all too much and so little at the same time. They briefly felt something soft against their arm.
•••••The commotion got louder after sometime. Riley rose from where they sat on the stretcher, letting the gusts of cool night air whisper against their skin through the open ambulance rear doors. Riley realizes they're not really as cold as they expected to be, and they look at their arms to inspect themselves. Their arms and some parts of their legs were bound in stained-red bandages, and for some unbeknownst reason, they weren't really shocked. Did they get into a fight with somebody again? Mommy's gonna be really upset if they did; they promised not to do it again unless they're being threatened.
They spot a paramedic nearby, tending to their maid. Oh. Did she get hurt too? That's not good. Maybe she got hurt when she was pouring the boiling hot tea Daddy likes. Daddy fired the last two maids that spilled his tea, poor maid. The nurse was kindly wrapping up the maid's hands. She probably spilled the hot tea on herself.
When Riley opened her mouth to call out to them, they found that their face felt tight. Reaching up a hand to feel their face, they flinch away when they feel hard bandages on their face as well. With trembling fingers, they reach out to touch their face again. It was bandaged, the material hard as they tap against it.
Something crumbles nearby, loud. They shakily hop off the stretcher, small, bare feet padding in the dirt towards unexpected warmth.Their chest tightened and their breathing picks up. The world closed down around them, yet warmth like no other bloomed inside their cool chest, taught to express nothing. Their eyes filled with fear but the corners of their lips twitch.Riley watched silently as their house burned, firefighters hosing down as much of it as possible, and the two covered bodies laying in front of it, with more people shaking their head, murmuring well wishes and condolences.It was heaven and hell, an impossible low and a never ending high.Freedom and yet even more trapped than they were before.
•••••The police declared the whole incident as an accident, a curtain catching fire from a nearby candle, or whatever. Riley knew what really happened. They lie on the bed, one of the few things salvaged, their unicorn plushie, in their arms. Everything else was burnt to a crisp. They didn't know anything yet, not about the length of their family tree, the value of money or how to tie their shoelace. Riley's eyes danced across the room, reimagining the fire that took their house and their parents.They wonder when Mommy and Daddy were coming back.

The summer that Liu Min learnt how to swim, in his first year of elementary school, Father brought them all for a seaside holiday. The rented villa was right on the shore, with its own private beach. Liu Min had learnt the word exclusivity by then, heard it most often from Mother: brand-name schools, closed-door boutiques, members-only restaurants. Something withheld that has to be earned.It was just– boring. Being on a beach without anyone to play with. Father stayed in the air-conditioned villa on his phone or laptop or other grown-up electronics; Mother stayed in the shade of a sun parasol.There was Liu Xiao, sure, but he hardly counted. Not for good company; barely for anything else. Anyway, the kid hadn’t learnt to swim yet, so it wasn’t even as if Liu Min could race him (and win, of course).By the end of their first day there, Liu Min was ready to leave. He was tired of the too-bright sun and how the sand clung to his flipflops. The sunset had been pretty, for a few minutes, but then they’d all had to go inside for dinner that the villa staff cooked for them. It hadn’t been anywhere as nice as the dinners that their own cook made at home. Liu Min had said so, laughing, expecting his parents to do the same – but they hadn’t. Mother had said something to the staff in the too-high voice she sometimes used on the phone. Father had looked ready to give him a lecture on etiquette.Liu Xiao had kept eating throughout the whole thing, quiet, not even looking up. For some reason, that annoyed Liu Min the most.Later, after the dishes had been cleared and the villa staff had left for the night, but before Father could deliver that probable lecture, Liu Min had slipped out of the villa – through the glass doors of the verandah, straight out onto the beach.The sky was still clear, with a half-moon and some scattered stars. He walked closer to the water. Further along the shore, he could see the bright lights of holiday resorts in the distance: the crowded, noisy type filled with ordinary people.He turned back, bored – and nearly yelped. Liu Xiao was standing behind him, silent and ghostlike.“What’s your problem?” Liu Min snapped.Liu Xiao looked at him, eyes wide and dark in his pale face. “Are you going for a swim?”“At night? You’re mad.”Something shifted in Liu Xiao’s gaze. Liu Min didn’t like it. It reminded him of how Father looked when he said Liu Min had to become more of a man. A look that said: You’re small, and weak, and scared.“Go swim by yourself,” Liu Min muttered. He strode towards Liu Xiao, shouldered roughly past him, half-hoping the kid would fall down.Liu Xiao didn’t. A soft sound – it could have been the wind, but Liu Min knew better. That brat was laughing.He whirled back around. “You think you’re so great, don’t you–”But Liu Xiao wasn’t looking at him. He was walking forward, unhurried and steady, towards the distant lapping of the waves. The little freak. Just showing off, obviously, pretending he was better than Liu Min, pretending he could do whatever Liu Min couldn’t.Liu Min watched as Liu Xiao reached the water’s edge. As he kept going.“Hey–” Liu Min said – broke off at the way his voice trembled, tried again: “Come back, you idiot, you’re going to get your clothes wet.”Liu Xiao kept going. Up to his ankles. Higher.“You crazy brat!” Liu Min was running before he knew it, splashing into the sea, grabbing Liu Xiao’s shoulder to spin him around. “Father’s going to–”Liu Xiao looked up at him.A faint breeze lifted the hair at the back of Liu Min’s neck. His skin prickled. The tide tugged at his legs, wave after wave, reminding him how much deeper the sea could go. He felt as if he was standing on the edge of something dark and vast and wild, something that could make him disappear without warning.Liu Xiao smiled. “Okay,” he said, placatory. “Let’s go.”

He was on billboards, a few campus shuttles, hell—probably someone’s phone wallpaper. Were colleges even allowed to show such blatant favoritism toward students in such a way?

New Balance.”Okay, while the line was kind of clean—it was just him that pissed you off. And it was insane because you never even met this guy to judge him. While you were in proximity to him, your best friends being cheerleaders and sharing the terrifyingly large court with them—you really had nothing bad to say about his character.

side, your hands in hers tracing invisible patterns on them as she leans her head on your shoulder. she can't see you. a vulnerability. one she doesn't let anyone else have. a show of trust and love. a way of saying "i'm here and ready to listen when you are ready to talk" without actually saying it.sue sits up in her robe on your other side turned towards you. she eyes you for a minute before scooting closer to lean your head on her without disrupting the redhead. snaking her arm around you while kissing your forehead tenderly. gentle strokes on the exposed skin of your scarred arm as a way to calm you. a whisper of "we've got you" is heard before her humming resumes. while she may not always be visible, the hums are a constant reassurance she's there. an act of vulnerability she The dropship lands with a tooth-rattling thud, and the sun assaults your eyes as soon as the landing ramp is deployed. You have to squint against the bright light just to keep yourself from tripping over your own feet as you and the other Marines tumble out onto the beach. You pause at the end of the ramp, closing your eyes and tilting your face toward the sun. It's a welcome change after the dark, dank atmosphere of Hadley's Hope. Soft, shuffling footsteps descend the ramp and come to a stop behind you. "I've never felt anything quite like it." He pauses multiple times to get more sunscreen for your left arm alone, and when you ask him about it, he murmurs, "I'm attempting to achieve even, effective coverage across all of your exposed skin." The sunscreen tube is almost empty by the time he's finished with you. You close your eyes as gentle fingers work the oily substance into your cheeks and forehead in precise little circles. Bishop is on his knees before you, back straight and hands resting idly on his thighs. Wide green eyes stare at you with such open affection that it's difficult to meet his gaze. D3rlord3's knees suddenly buckle with a shudder, armor meeting stone with a grating shriek.*You are afraid. You need not be.He is not afraid. He is not afraid. He is not.His King's hands (so, so wrong. in all ways, so wrong) slide under his helmet and up to his jaw, cradling it as one would something broken.He looms over D3rlord3, that inky black void resting over his visage. Somehow, he can tell a smile is under it.D3rlord3 hopes he never has to see behind the black veil ever again.*So cruel. Am I unsightly?"Yes."(No. The King was the most beautiful thing D3rlord3 had ever seen in his life. All encompassing, lethal with glory, and dripping with utter, raw, truth.)*You are shaking.So he is. D3rlord3's armor lightly clatters together, his hands shivering with fear.Fear?No, he is not scared. He is not afraid.His King smooths his cheeks out with His (wrong, wrong, wrong) hands, stroking over them in caressing circles, akin to worship.*Indulge me.D3rlord's breath hitches as his world turns yellow.Gone was the stone of the mine, here was the color of truth.Silken robes sweep him up, wrap around him like millions of arms, and clutch him close to His chest.*You deserve a rest.No, no, no. vessel quiets.*His

Will tells himself he isn’t going to look at Mike.He’s been telling himself that his whole life, actually, and ever since being stuck back in Hawkins he’s actually been… decent at it. He sticks close to Jonathan most of the time when they’re at the Wheeler home, and hangs out with both Mike and Holly to avoid being alone with him. Mike’s been busy too, figuring out how to deal with Hawkins being monitored the way it is. Will is doing good, but he slips three times tonight – first when they climb down into the half-collapsed maintenance hatch and Mike reaches for his hand to steady him, then when Dustin and Lucas argue loudly enough to shake dust from the ceiling in the tunnels, and again when Mike brushes past him in the cramped space and Will’s lungs forget how to function.He isn’t supposed to feel like this. Not now, not with El out there, fighting for her life. Not when Vecna might still be waiting somewhere in the shadows. Not when Mike is… Mike. Brave. Smart. Handsome.These feelings aren’t new. Will knows that. He’s felt this way about Mike even before he knew what it was. Just one more item on the ever-growing list of reasons he hates himself. Sometimes, Will thinks it would’ve been easier if he hadn’t made it out of the Upside Down at all. Other times – when he’s really feeling dark – he’s grateful for the war, for the chaos. It’s sick and rotten and he hates himself for it, but fighting monsters is easier than sitting with these feelings. Easier than talking about them. Easier than admitting that the only person he wants to talk to is the one person he can’t.A steady drip echoes through the tunnel. Will keeps his eyes fixed on the ground, sneakers sinking into packed dirt, toes brushing over rusted pipes. The air smells metallic, stale. Every so often, a low tremor hums through the floor – a reminder of where they are, what they’re hiding from, what they need to do.Dustin leads the way, flashlight beam jerking wildly with every animated gesture. Lucas walks beside him, arguing pointlessly about structural integrity.And Mike –Well, Mike is next to Will.Too close.Close enough that Will can hear him breathing. Close enough that their shoulders brush whenever the walls narrow. Close enough that Will’s stupid, ugly heart keeps hammering like it’s trying to claw its way out.He tries to focus on the mission. Really, he does.But Mike starts to slow down to match his pacing, which means their arms are brushing every other second now. Dustin starts arguing with Lucas about whether tunnels grown by an interdimensional hive mind can “technically collapse,” and Will feels Mike shift beside him – the kind of shift that usually means Mike’s about to step in, mediate, scold, lead.
The tunnels widen as they go, branching into uneven corridors that twist like broken ribs. Dustin mutters something about choosing the “least murder-y path,” but Will barely hears him – the low psychic hum he’s been feeling since they entered finally fades into nothing.He exhales, tension loosening a fraction.“Guys, the signal’s gone,” he murmurs. “Vecna. I don’t feel him. Not right now.”Dustin slows. “Gone gone? Or, like, smoke-break gone?”Will shrugs. “I don’t know. But… it feels safe for the moment.”Lucas squints into the dark ahead. “Yeah? Doesn’t look safe.”“It’s safer than it was,” Will says. “Which is the best we’re gonna get.”Dustin huffs. Lucas huffs louder. And somehow that tiny difference sets them off again.Will barely notices how quiet Mike has become until the front-row argument fizzles. Dustin and Lucas bicker over something stupid–map orientation, maybe, or whether the “safe route” is actually safe–but behind them, Mike hasn’t spoken in minutes. That alone is unusual. Mike Wheeler never lets an argument linger for more than ten seconds without jumping in to referee.Will slows his steps.Mike’s shoulders are tight, hunched. Something in his walk looks wrong – too rigid, too careful. For a second Will thinks Mike’s hurt, that he twisted an ankle or something in the last tunnel bend.Then Mike wipes his face.Quick and sharp. Back of his hand across his cheekbone. And then again. And again.Will stops walking entirely.Because Mike – bossy, stubborn, steady-in-a-crisis Mike – is crying. Silently. Continuously.Will’s breath catches. Mike looks up, then looks away. Will opens his mouth and Mike shakes his head instantly, violently, like the question physically touches him. “Don’t.” He hiccups out, thick and tight. He doesn’t even look at Will. Just keeps on walking.Will’s stomach drops. No one cries like that unless they have absolutely no control left.Okay. Okay. Think.He turns to Lucas and Dustin. “Hey – uh – can you guys go check the next path? Like fifty feet ahead? Just make sure it’s still clear?”Both Dustin and Lucas turn around, eyes widening when they see the current state. “Oh,” Dustin says awkwardly. “Uh.”Lucas’ expression softens, eyes wide with concern. “Mike, man, you okay?”Mike squeezes his eyes shut, nodding his head

It started as yet another long, boring day at the agency. Atsushi rubbed his temple with the eraser of his pencil, blinking groggily at the bright computer screen. The case they were working on was unsurprisingly dreadful, just as every case was. Atsushi tried to stay positive, don’t get him wrong. It was just that he was really tired. It was rough dealing with whatever mess Yokohama was in every two days. That and the fact that he’d been working since 7AM and it was now 9PM. Maybe he should take a break and circle back tomorrow. Everyone was basically gone except for him anyway. He made enough headway today, right?
He sighed tiredly as he pushed his chair back from the desk, just about to power off his computer when he jolted at the sudden bang of the rather flimsy agency door. The glass almost cracked a little on the impact. It wasn’t that the door banging in such a way was peculiar. Kunikida had a habit of doing that whenever a certain brunette pissed him off so much he needed to take five. (To take Kunikida from work like that sure was a special ability of its own.) But no, it was the fact that Dazai was the one doing the slamming. Sure Dazai got irritated like anyone else, but his agitation was almost always veiled by a thin smile and clever tongue. Atsushi has never seen Dazai show such…emotion. Of course his first instinct was to wonder if he was the reason behind this odd change—that this was somehow his fault—but the second he opened his mouth to speak, Dazai was already speaking himself.
“Well, dearest, I thoroughly apologize for ruining your oh-so perfect schedule. It’s not my fault you can’t take two minutes out of your day.”
Atsushi was about to question what Dazai was talking about, or why he was calling him “dearest” of all things, but that was until his eyes landed on the flip phone pressed against Dazai’s ear.Oh, so he was on the phone with someone then. He seemed so focused on the conversation too—odd considering he has a tendency to not give a fuck about most of the conversations he’s in. This person truly grasped his attention to the point where Dazai didn’t even notice Atsushi was still there. For some reason, Atsushi felt the urge to duck under the desk in that moment. It felt like if he was noticed at this point, he’d be shamed for eavesdropping, even if he had no control of the situation.
Just who was it…?
Atsushi slapped his cheeks lightly, which were now slightly warm from embarrassment. Just what was he thinking!? That was completely and entirely Dazai’s business. Then again, it’s not like he could stop his ears from hearing…the only reason he’s still hiding here is so that Dazai doesn’t get the wrong idea. Yeah, that’s it. If he hears anything it’s purely by accident and unintentional. Wrong place wrong time—that sort of deal.
“You couldn’t have told Mori something came up? It’s not like he doesn’t have other men,” Dazai pouts as he plops down on a chair and kicks his feet up on the desk. It was no surprise he did this in the spot that was self-proclaimed as Kunikida’s.
Atsushi was thoroughly confused now. Mori? As in the Port Mafia boss, Mori? He couldn’t help but jump to the worst conclusions. Was Dazai in close contact with the enemy? Well…okay…the Port Mafia was hardly considered enemy at this point, not with how many times they’ve allied with the Agency. But still! Mafia=bad guys. Dazai+mafia=bad guy..? This was hurting Atsushi’s brain. He should have faith in Dazai. Everything he did had intention and purpose. If he was getting tangled up with someone in the Port Mafia, there had to be a reasonable explanation, right? Yeah…

I do not enjoy it when Constance is unsettled, and there is no point to any of it, if I do not enjoy it.Should Constance follow me, there will be no point to any of it if she does not enjoy it as well. Paris shakes and heaves under the weight of fire, plague, revolt, construction projects forever ripping out the city's ancient guts. Armand stands in the center of it all, distant and remote as a stolen obelisk. Paris looks at him and sees whatever it wants to see.He holds the coven on a firm leash during the Revolution, leading them beneath the guillotines to lap drops of noble blood. In the years of the Commune he keeps the plays going, entertaining first the bright-eyed Communards and then the soldiers who slaughter them. Liberty, equality, fraternity is just another dull slogan.The Nazis come and fill the audience, cheering for chocolate-flavored bloodshed while the Resistance scurries beneath their feet. Drunken soldiers clamber up the balcony and Armand lets them pull at his clothes and hair, gnawing at his skin with their blunt teeth. It’s a nostalgic kind of surrender, really.After the war, whispers of collaborators stain their doorway, so their audience slacks off, save the profoundly bored or profoundly loyal. Baby Lulu helps the audience forget, at least before she ends up on trial. A reminder that the cruelty never left, even if the swastikas did.Armand scrapes Paris out of his accent after he leaves, drains French from his tongue, stubbornly memorizes the maps of new cities. In 1968 he watches television footage of youth tearing up cobblestones, shaking the city with their yowling discontent. It peters out soon, as most revolutions do. Mortals always underestimate how very exhausting it is to fight back.Nearly a century after he abandoned his city, Armand slips into the warehouse where the museum thieves have hidden away with their treasures. He picks over their bodies afterward and wonders if this counts as patriotism, or simply a side effect of loneliness; Paris cannot reject his offerings, unlike the rest of his old lovers.Armand leaves most of the jewels at the Louvre's door, except for the emerald necklace. He thinks he’s earned himself a keepsake or two.

On 5 June, precisely at 4:35 in the afternoon, sprawled across the carpet of Grimmauld Place, Harry thought with startling clarity: “I have to marry him.” It wasn’t a thought that came out of nowhere. Perhaps it was because Draco was hitting just the right spot at that very moment, the way the blond breathed, the way he looked at him while claiming him. Yes, that was probably what was unsettling the green-eyed man.He said nothing, but all he could think about was how much he loved him. When they were finished and Draco drifted off to sleep, Harry lay awake, staring at the blond hair peeking out from beneath the sheets. It felt right. Perhaps he was exaggerating. They weren’t teenagers sneaking around anymore; in fact, they had been together for twelve years—at least in Harry’s mind, who counted from the day he first met Draco. He swore that blond had always been his. In reality, their relationship had only been official for three years.He still remembered his friends’ ridiculous reactions when he confessed he was mad about Malfoy.— “And that’s new for you?” Hermione had teased.— “Giving up Quidditch for Draco Malfoy could only mean you wanted to shag him, mate.” Ron had said, face twisted in disgust.But it wasn’t a real problem. Draco had changed astonishingly. He was still sarcastic and mocking, but also helpful and a good listener. He had even won Hermione over when his thesis for qualifying as a Healer proved so fascinating that everyone urged him to publish it as a book. Ron often joked that both he and Harry were the idiots in the relationship. Harry didn’t think himself an idiot. Practical, perhaps. And he didn’t mind not being the cleverest one—rarely did he have to worry about anything, and the saviour of the wizarding world was grateful for that.His thoughts were interrupted when a drowsy Draco shifted, turning his back to him. “Grave mistake, Draco Malfoy,” Harry thought, moving closer to pepper kisses across his body. He never quite got used to that strong, masculine silhouette, that intoxicating scent—a mix of sex and expensive cologne. Merlin, he loved him.—“Can’t sleep?”—murmured Draco, half-awake. Harry melted on the spot. A simple question, yet every ordinary thing Draco did drove him mad.—“May I ask you something?”—Harry ventured, knowing Draco was practically asleep. The blond didn’t reply, which was better. Harry could speak without embarrassment.—“If I were to propose something as mad as marriage, would you say yes, or call me a traditionalist fool?”No answer came.—Love.My life. My everything. Draco… Lucius…– Harry whispered.
—“Don’t… call me that” 
Draco muttered, barely conscious. —“But you’d say yes…”The blond gave a sleepy grunt that Harry took as assent.—“And if, hypothetically, I asked how you’d like me to—”—“Harry.” Draco sat up suddenly, hair tousled, eyes barely open yet still devastatingly handsome. “You should know I’m not listening. I’ve got to leave at eight in the morning and it’s…”—he conjured a tempus—“four o’clock. Could you wait until dawn?”—“Oh, yes, of course,” Harry replied quickly, feigning indifference. It confirmed his suspicion that Draco hadn’t paid attention, which was a relief. He had nearly regretted asking how he might propose.Marriage.The thought struck him again. Draco turned back over, and Harry simply wrapped his arms around him, kissed his hair, and stayed still. The feeling of Draco in his embrace, after a day of endless lovemaking, was overwhelming. He was with the love of his life.His family—the Weasleys—adored him. Hermione always sought his help with baffling potions, Ron looked forward to Friday nights to challenge Draco at chess. Their relationship was steady: they never went to bed angry, they understood each other. But Harry was greedy. He wanted more. Physical closeness wasn’t enough. Sometimes he begged Draco to stay inside him while they slept, unable to bear the emptiness when he withdrew. That had led to confusion, even fear, with Draco worrying he had hurt him. Harry buried his face in the hollow of Draco’s neck and shoulder, breathing him in.Draco was real. He could smell him, feel him.And he wanted more. He wanted to see a ring on that beautiful hand.He would think of something.
